substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L03 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in simple social or routine learning activities by relying on key words, paralinguistic (non-verbal) communication and context

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing formulas or short exchanges, based on models, for example ‘Hello, what is your name?’, ‘My name is … What is your name?’ and ‘Pleased to meet you.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using social formulas, for example ‘please’, ‘thank you’ and ‘excuse me’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using learnt phrases in different situations, for example ‘What’s the time?’, ‘Oh, no!’ and ‘Very good!’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions about an experience or text in simple ways, for example ‘I like.’ and ‘Not good.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common vocabulary related to personal and social needs (such as ‘toilet’, ‘pencil’ and ‘stop’) and constructing simple phrases with this vocabulary, for example ‘Go toilet?’, ‘This my pencil.’ and ‘Stop that!’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L03-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using picture cards, classroom charts and objects to enhance communication; for example, pointing to a picture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L04 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: follow a sequence of simple utterances, with teacher and contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding a simple spoken text when accompanied by visual support, for example for instructions for and demonstration of a game or art activity

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating how to make or do something with some accompanying words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L04-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing popular stories or songs such as Goldilocks and the Three Bears

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L05 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise familiar spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L05-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying familiar spoken texts used frequently in class, such as songs, rhymes and stories

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L05-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared oral reading of familiar texts; for example, joining in the chorus or saying a repeated line from a familiar text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L06 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a small range of simple sentence patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common time references in basic sentences, for example in ‘We went yesterday.’, ‘We will go tomorrow.’ and ‘Now we can eat lunch.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing to people or illustrations when responding to questions or instructions using gendered personal pronouns such as ‘him’ or ‘her’ or possessive pronouns such as ‘his’ or ‘her’, for example pointing and saying, ‘That is him.’ and ‘There is her bag.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L06-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gendered pronouns with accuracy some of the time, for example in ‘He is my dad.’ and ‘She is my aunty.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L07 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: construct simple subject–verb–object sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L07-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching simple verb tense to time words, for example in ‘Yesterday we did …’ and ‘Tomorrow we will do …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ‘no’ or ‘not’ with adjectives or nouns to express negation, for example in ‘Not finished.’ and ‘Not cold today.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L08 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: demonstrate variable placement of common adjectives and adverbs to describe or add emphasis

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a small range of common adjectives, for example in ‘the big house’ and ‘smelly socks’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining some common adverbs with verbs to describe action, with varying degrees of accuracy, for example in ‘walk slowly’ and ‘sing good’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common adverbs to vary the intensity of adjectives, for example in ‘very hot’ and ‘little bit funny’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L09 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use words related to immediate communicative needs, interests or experiences

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L09-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key words and phrases that refer to familiar objects in the classroom, for example in ‘Please pass glue stick.’ and ‘Hang bag on hook.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L09-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a single word for a variety of purposes; for example, using ‘book’ to mean ‘This is my book.’, ‘Where is her book?’ or ‘I’d like to borrow that book.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L09-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to classroom charts and a simple personal vocabulary list to identify, clarify and rehearse words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L09-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of strategies to embed learnt words and phrases in their own speech and writing, for example as private rehearsal and a simple personal vocabulary list

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L10 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use comprehensible pronunciation to blend, segment and manipulate familiar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and producing rhyming words when listening to rhyming stories or rhymes, for example ‘funny’ and ‘money’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying patterns of alliteration in known spoken words, for example ‘helpful Hasma’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying a word when given the sounds, for example ‘lip’ for ‘l-i-p’ and ‘munch’ for ‘m-u-n-ch’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying whether sounds are the same or different; for example, comparing the vowel sounds in ‘ship’ and ‘sheep’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying an unfamiliar word when the beginning phoneme (the smallest unit of sound in a word), middle or end phoneme is replaced with a different phoneme; for example, ‘run’ becomes ‘fun’ and ‘fun’ becomes ‘fan’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L10-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying syllables in known spoken words, for example clapping the rhythm of ‘Mon-day’, ‘Ti-en’ or ‘A-si-ma’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L11 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise ways that sentence stress and intonation are used to enhance meaning or distinguish statements from questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L11-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that a question has been asked, based on intonation

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L11-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising emotions such as happiness and anger expressed through intonation

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L11-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between questions, instructions and statements based on clear intonation and contextual information, for example in the actions of peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L11-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using rising intonation for questions and stressing key words for emphasis

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L12 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise when to respond in English and when to respond in home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L12-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising when being spoken to in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L12-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: assessing which language(s) a speaker knows, and responding appropriately

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L12-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between new English words and home language words containing similar sounds

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L13 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple strategies to clarify spoken communication and respond to misunderstandings

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L13-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting attention or assistance from the teacher or a peer by using intonation to signal a request, or indicating non-understanding through speech or body language

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L13-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple formulaic expressions to ask for clarification, for example ‘Please say again.’ and ‘What is that?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L13-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and using a speaker’s key words when asking for clarification; for example, Teacher: ‘Paste it in your book.’ Student: ‘Language book?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L14 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources to enhance learning when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L14-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers for help with translating personal needs and responses from a home language to English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L14-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L14-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification from other home language speakers

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1L15 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of simple social formulas and gestures to interact with others orally

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L15-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that words, gestures and intonations may be appropriate or inappropriate in certain contexts; for example, saying ‘please’ when asking for something from a peer

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L15-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating that they are paying attention through paralinguistic (non-verbal) communication; for example, using body orientation, nodding, gesturing and facial expressions such as smiling and laughing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L15-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding when a response is required and attempting to respond appropriately to questions by using a variety of paralinguistic (non-verbal) communication and/or short responses

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1L15-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recalling and using common social formulas when interacting with others; for example, saying ‘sorry’, ‘please’, ‘thank you’ and ‘excuse me’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R01 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the main themes or ideas of short, familiar print and digital texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R01-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: scanning texts for familiar words and short phrases in context; for example, looking for the names of main characters or key topic vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R01-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the main ideas of short texts about a topic studied in class and responding to questions; for example, naming characters from a story or identifying an animal illustration based on a description

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R01-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating comprehension through appropriate activities; for example, retelling the main ideas from a text, sequencing pictures representing the main events in a story, or painting or drawing events, settings or characters in a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R02 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify key information in simple, familiar texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R02-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising illustrations or character names when re-reading a familiar story

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R02-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying characters, settings or key events in a narrative

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R02-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying or recounting one or 2 facts from a non-fiction text, for example ‘Sharks have sharp teeth.’ and ‘Cars have 4 wheels.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R03 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: match images to familiar words and phrases, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the meaning of everyday signs and labels such as a stop sign on a road and an exit sign near a door

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming some familiar logos or symbols such as a common emoji

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying characters or objects that are represented in both images and print text; for example, noticing a familiar cartoon character

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching a short description to an image, for example for ‘a green fruit’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R04 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: make simple predictions or inferences about a text, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple predictions about the topic or purpose of a text based on the introduction, for example about the purpose of an instructional video

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using images on a book cover or illustrations within the text to predict what might happen next

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R04-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: finishing familiar phrases or sentences from known texts; for example, joining in a repeated chorus or refrain within a familiar text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R05 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise the basic features of different types of texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising a small range of familiar text types such as recount, narrative, instructional report and information report

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions about the features of a text, for example when asked ‘What is the name of this text?’ and ‘Where is there a list in this text?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching labels to parts of a simple text, for example to the title, introduction, requirements and method of a procedure; the title, images and text on a poster; and the text, hyperlinks and images on a website

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: following step-by-step instructions to find information in a print or digital text in response to a question, for example when asked ‘Open the book and turn to the contents page. Now find the heading that says “Ocean”. Which page should we turn to?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and naming elements of book layout and aspects of reading such as word, letter, page, title and cover

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R05-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing to parts of a book in response to questions and instructions, for example when asked ‘What is the author’s name?’ and ‘Find the start of the sentence.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R06 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise a range of familiar words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising personally significant words, for example when seeing their own name on charts, book labels and name tags

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating and pointing to familiar words or phrases when prompted, for example when asked ‘This book is about frogs. Where can you see the word “frog”?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R06-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning that words are made up of meaningful parts, for example that ‘dogs’ has 2 meaningful parts: ‘dog’ and ‘s’ (meaning ‘more than one’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R06-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar high-frequency words such as ‘and’, ‘my’, ‘is’, ‘the’ and ‘go’ in shared and independent reading texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R07 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify some sounds in words, and some common letters and letter patterns in words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising letters in recurring words, for example in the names of peers and teachers

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching upper-case and lower-case letters and identifying their sounds

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: relating some letters of the alphabet to their common sounds; for example, relating vowels to their short vowel sound

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using initial letters and common letter patterns to decode unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating words containing the same letter patterns in a short text, for example in words containing ‘ch’ or all words with double letters

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R07-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that different ways of forming letters and different fonts do not change meaning

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R08 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the function of capital letters, spaces and full stops

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: pausing at full stops when reading aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spaces to identify and count words in a sentence or on a line

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that capital letters and full stops can form sentence boundaries, and can be used to identify and count sentences

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R09 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: distinguish print and digital English texts from home language texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R09-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a text written in English or pointing to English words in a multilingual text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R09-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: holding and navigating English books appropriately and confidently

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R09-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the intended audience of English and home language texts, for example in ‘This story is for children.’ and ‘This book is for adults.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R10 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select suitable texts for their own reading, with teacher and peer support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R10-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting and engaging with books of personal interest during independent reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R10-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring a new book before reading to determine interest, by looking at the images, amount of print and familiar elements

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R10-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking books in a home language or related to familiar topics to share with family members

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R10-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with picture books selected by the teacher and some self-selected books

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R11 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources to enhance learning when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R11-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers for help with translating personal needs and responses from a home language to English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R11-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R11-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to picture dictionaries or bilingual dictionaries in the classroom to check meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R11-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple multilingual mind maps or vocabulary charts of key words

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1R12 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in shared reading activities, including reading aloud, with extensive teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to a teacher or peer read text aloud, then rehearsing and imitating pronunciation, intonation and emphasis

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading aloud short, familiar texts such as simple rhymes, songs and repetitive texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading short texts aloud, with prompts from the teacher, for example for their own writing or a story or text used in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions about their personal experiences related to stories, for example when asked ‘Have you ever … ?’ and ‘Do you like … too?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a simple opinion on a text; for example, indicating like or dislike of a character

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1R12-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to shared responses to texts; for example, sequencing images in order, matching sentence stems and endings, answering simple questions about ideas in a text and acting out events

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1W01 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write familiar words, phrases or short texts and write simple functional texts related to their own experience or school context, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing or typing familiar words such as their own name, without copying

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing the names of items depicted in images or captions for images

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing short formulaic sentences to describe images, for example ‘This is a …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing sentences giving personal information, for example ‘My name is …’ and ‘I have … people in my family.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recounting personal experiences in sequence

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a simple description, recount or procedure after a shared class experience, for example as a short text recounting how to make toast

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W01-E07 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a simple response to a familiar text; for example, using characters or a setting from a familiar story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1W02 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: illustrate a simple text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W02-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating a simple text to add detail, for example to give additional information about an event, character or setting in a story

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W02-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using drawings as a basis for spoken explanations or captioning using simple writing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1W03 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a simple, familiar text structure repeatedly

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing or dictating simple statements in time sequence, for example ‘I get my bag.’ and ‘I eat lunch.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing recounts or stories using repetitive time or sequence connectives, for example ‘First I …, then I …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a teacher-modelled planner to write a simple narrative text with a beginning–middle–end structure

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a variety of text features, for example by placing text appropriately on a page, leaving space for a drawing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA1W04 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write simple, repetitive modelled sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a small range of sentences copied from a model text, for example ‘I like …’, ‘I went to …’ and ‘Today is …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA1W04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple strings of words that approximate their own spoken structures, for example ‘go to school’, ‘go home’ and ‘come from’, although they may demonstrate errors or inconsistency in grammar and word order

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level A2 curriculum supports students who may have already had several years of age-appropriate formal instruction in the basics of English language and literacy, and some exposure to home language literacy, to expand their repertoire of spoken and written English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students explore spoken communication in predictable social situations. Students learn to identify key points in familiar topics and develop their capacity to use images as cues to decode meaning. They learn how to negotiate and sustain spoken interaction and resolve misunderstandings by using a range of resources, including home language(s).

Students explore a wide range of familiar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. With support, they learn to read familiar texts such as everyday texts and short literary texts with some fluency. They practise strategies such as referring to a picture or home language–English bilingual dictionary to check the spelling or meaning of English words. They also learn about context, phoneme–grapheme correspondences, word patterns and text structure, which assist with reading unfamiliar texts. Students explore the writing process to develop the knowledge, understanding and skills involved in planning a short written text. They create their own texts using simple, coherently linked sentences, basic structures and familiar vocabulary. They are introduced to unfamiliar words and learn about spelling patterns and base words as a way of broadening their vocabularies. Students develop and improve their own writing through engaging in discussion of simple stories, recounts and factual texts.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level A2, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students communicate in a range of predictable and familiar social and learning situations. They express ideas and identify key points of information in classroom discussions about familiar topics, and about new topics when they are well supported by visual material, an appropriate pace of delivery, and discussion that links their prior knowledge to the new context. They follow a short sequence of instructions related to classroom procedures and learning activities. They negotiate familiar social and learning situations, using English appropriate to the situation. They adjust their speech choices in response to audiences and topics. They combine known conversational formulas and vocabulary, including some from texts read in class, and apply grammatical rules to make original utterances of varying grammatical accuracy. They sustain communication by negotiating turn-taking and by using strategies such as asking a speaker to repeat or to speak slowly, or by asking what a word means.

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating a range of familiar situations; for example, explaining a problem to a teacher, negotiating the rules of a game with a friend, participating in a class discussion, describing an object and ordering food at the school canteen

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in classroom discussions about familiar topics or new topics that are well supported by visual material and/or scaffolding provided by the teacher

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in short, structured social interactions; for example, understanding and responding to simple questions related to personal or familiar topics by borrowing words from questions asked, such as responding ‘My hobby is …’ to ‘What is your hobby?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple requests and expressing needs, thoughts and opinions; for example, making formulaic requests such as ‘Can I have a pencil, please?’ and indicating agreement or non-agreement such as saying ‘I agree.’ or ‘I don’t think so.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing ideas, humour and simple opinions, and describing feelings, for example ‘I am very happy.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common classroom formulaic responses, for example ‘Just a minute.’, ‘Can you help me, please?’, ‘Be quiet, please.’ and ‘Can I have a paintbrush, please?’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L06 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a small range of sentence forms, including common time and sequence markers to link speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common forms of statements (e.g. for those starting with ‘I am …’ and ‘This is …’) and the difference between statements and commands (e.g. between ‘She went home.’ and ‘Please give it to me.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using a variety of question stems such as ‘Who’, ‘Where’, ‘How’, ‘Why’, ‘Do you’ and ‘Can I’ (e.g. ‘Where did you live before?’) and yes/no questions (e.g. ‘Is that my book?’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common conjunctions that make connections between ideas, for example in ‘I like my dog and taking him for a walk is fun.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions that include sequence markers such as ‘first’, ‘next’, ‘and then’ and ‘after that’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using simple time markers such as ‘yesterday’, ‘later’ and ‘now’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L07 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a small range of common verb forms accurately

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing subject–verb–object sentences with accuracy, for example ‘I brushed my teeth.’ and ‘She threw the ball.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some forms of the verbs ‘to be’ and ‘to have’ correctly, for example ‘is’ in ‘Her name is Mia.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of common verb tenses for familiar verbs with some consistency; for example, using present simple tense (such as ‘walk’ and ‘go’), present continuous tense (such as ‘is walking’ and ‘is going’) and regular and common irregular past tenses (such as ‘walked’ and ‘went’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning commands with an imperative verb, for example in ‘Come over here, please.’ and ‘Bring me that book, please.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to recognise and use basic modal verbs, for example in ‘want to’, ‘have to’ and ‘should’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple negation using common auxiliary verbs such as ‘don’t’, ‘did not’ and ‘can’t’ in full and contracted forms, for example ‘The bus did not come.’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L08 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a number of different phrase forms

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving some additional detail using short noun groups or adjectival phrases, for example in ‘He gave me a new book.’ and ‘I ran really fast.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding some common phrases or clauses in both their full and contracted forms, for example ‘I am’ and ‘I’m’, ‘you are’ and ‘you’re’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common prepositions such as ‘in’, ‘on’ and ‘at’ to add simple detail about place, for example in ‘Go on the train.’ and ‘Stay at home.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding instructions incorporating place or location, for example for ‘Come over here.’ and ‘Stand next to the chair.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of personal pronouns such as ‘I’, ‘me’, ‘he’, ‘him’, ‘she’, ‘they’ and ‘it’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of possessive pronouns such as ‘his’, ‘her’, ‘its’, ‘our’, ‘their’ and ‘my’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L15 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: initiate and maintain simple spoken interactions with others

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating activities with peers in small-group tasks, for example by making suggestions, agreeing, disagreeing or clarifying

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding with short extended responses, including answering questions, adding to other speakers’ points and giving personal opinions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating meaning by using gestures, modified speech, simple questions and clarifications

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L01-E03 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L01-E04 - EAL Pathway A

content_descriptions.text: use a range of stress and intonation patterns to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E01 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E02 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E03 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using body language, facial expressions and gestures to enhance the meaning of speech, such as nodding and pointing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E05 - EAL Pathway A

modes.mode_body: Students read and respond to a wide range of familiar print or digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They predict, ask questions, retell and talk about texts read and viewed in class. With support, students read a range of topic-related classroom texts. They can read familiar texts with some fluency. They read back their own writing or their own sentences recorded by another student. They use texts purposefully, following simple procedural texts and finding basic information in texts. They discuss the events and characters’ feelings and actions in texts. They identify the purposes of familiar text types, including classroom text, simple story and factual text. They use their developing knowledge of context, phoneme–grapheme correspondences, word patterns and text structure to read simple texts, both familiar and unfamiliar. They interpret simple images and identify the layout of a range of text types.

modes.mode_body: Students communicate ideas, events and experiences through simple texts based on familiar spoken and written language. They write for a variety of personal and classroom purposes, using known and modelled structures and features. They write everyday texts and simple stories, recounts and factual texts based on their own and shared class experiences. They use their developing oral and reading skills when writing their own texts. They write texts using simple but coherently linked sentences, basic structures and well-known vocabulary. They use some common irregular past tense verbs correctly, and link clauses using basic conjunctions and connectives. They make plausible attempts to spell unfamiliar words, based on known spelling patterns and base words. They use vocabulary lists, modelled texts and familiar books to find out how to write unfamiliar words. They write letters legibly, include some punctuation and make some changes to their texts when editing. They use digital resources to write and present their texts.

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W10-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning the layout and format of a text, for example by ruling margins, writing and measuring out boxes on a poster or separating ideas in the text by leaving a line or writing a heading

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W10-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing legibly and consistently by hand, using a range of implements such as pens and pencils for different purposes

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W10-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying topic sentences or parts of sentences to support idea generation and to structure writing using words, phrases or sentence patterns from a teacher-modelled text, a favourite story or a home language text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W10-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a short, basic text type, following the structure of a model text, for example by copying sentence beginnings in the same order using spoken-like language structures based on familiar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W10-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating images close to relevant written information; for example, placing images near relevant headings or text in a digital text

as_extracts.name: EEALA2-E22
as_extracts.description: They write texts using simple but coherently linked sentences, basic structures and well-known vocabulary.

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W03 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: use a variety of simple text structures

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the purpose of a text, for example to inform, to describe an event or to tell a story

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing a small range of common text types, for example as a narrative, recount, report, procedure, description and explanation, reflecting the vocabulary and structure of spoken English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using templates or model texts for organisational structure; for example, using an introduction, body paragraphs and a conclusion (with less reliance on directly copying a reference text)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping short sentences about the same topic to produce an original text, for example ‘Frogs are green. Frogs have big eyes. They eat insects.’, or writing a series of short statements in time sequence, for example ‘I eat breakfast. I go to school. I read a book.’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W04 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: write sustained texts using sentences based on simple, repetitive, modelled patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic conjunctions and connectives to show time and sequence, for example in ‘On Saturday I … We went … We saw … I went … Then I … And then …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting clauses to make compound sentences that may run on, for example in ‘I came to school and met my friend and then we played handball and then the bell went.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W04-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ‘because’ to create dependent clauses, although these may be incomplete sentences, for example in ‘We went to the pool. Because it was hot.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W04-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting clauses into basic compound or complex sentences using common conjunctions such as ‘and’, ‘but’, ‘and then’, ‘because’ and ‘so’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W04-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple pronoun references to avoid repeating the subject in consecutive sentences, for example in ‘Ahmed came to school early. He felt very tired.’ and ‘Yesterday the class went … We went …’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W06 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: write common nouns and adjectives in the correct order in formulaic structures

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: building short noun phrases using adjectives, for example ‘the blue car’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple comparative adjectives in basic sentences with varying accuracy, for example in ‘My brother is bigger than me.’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W07 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: use high-frequency words encountered in classroom activities

elaborations.elaboration_text: using learnt topic-specific vocabulary in simple modelled sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: building word families from common morphemes (meaningful units within words), for example ‘play’, ‘plays’, ‘playing’, ‘played’ and ‘playground’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W07-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using morphemes to read words; for example, recognising the base word in words such as ‘walk-ed’

as_extracts.name: EEALA2-E23

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W05 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: use a small range of basic verb forms accurately

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W05-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common, simple past tense forms with the suffix ‘-ed’ consistently, although overgeneralising rules for some less common irregular past tense verbs (such as in ‘catched’, ‘freezed’ and ‘waked’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W05-E02 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W05-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using more complex tenses inconsistently, for example in ‘I have never eat it before.’ and ‘We caught the train then walk to the park.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W05-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some common imperatives appropriately, for example ‘Draw …’, ‘Stop.’, ‘Mix the …’ and ‘Cook the …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W05-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple negative constructions accurately, for example ‘I do not like …’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W08 - EAL Pathway A
content_descriptions.text: accurately spell familiar words and words with common letter patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of letters and sounds to spell words with short vowels (such as in ‘man’) and with common long vowel sounds (such as in ‘time’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of letter sounds to spell one-syllable words with consonant digraphs and consonant blends, such as ‘wish’ and ‘rest’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: spelling high-frequency words correctly, including words with regular and irregular spelling components and common function words (such as ‘the’, ‘and’, ‘is’ and ‘it’) as well as one- and 2-syllable words with common letter patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W08-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying similar spelling patterns, for example in words that contain the same letter combinations, such as in ‘find’ and ‘finger’, ‘air’ and ‘chair’

content_descriptions.text: use some punctuation consistently

elaborations.elaboration_text: correcting capital letters and full stops when reviewing their own or others’ writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W09-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with other punctuation such as quotation marks

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L01-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding when listening by displaying appropriate body language; for example, using body orientation, eye contact and facial expressions and gestures such as nodding or shaking their head

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L01-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing relevant comments or ideas when responding to a spoken text; for example, providing a basic response to a question about the spoken text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L01-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using images or other information to understand the meaning of a spoken text; for example, making a connection between an image and a short statement from a spoken text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L02-E01 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L02-E02 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L02-E05 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E01 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E02 - EAL Pathway A

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in short, structured social interactions; for example, understanding and responding to simple questions related to personal or familiar topics by borrowing words from questions asked, such as responding ‘My hobby is …’ to ‘What is your hobby?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple requests and expressing needs, thoughts and opinions; for example, making formulaic requests such as ‘Can I have a pencil, please?’ and indicating agreement or non-agreement such as saying ‘I agree.’ or ‘I don’t think so.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing ideas, humour and simple opinions, and describing feelings, for example ‘I am very happy.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L03-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common classroom formulaic responses, for example ‘Just a minute.’, ‘Can you help me, please?’, ‘Be quiet, please.’ and ‘Can I have a paintbrush, please?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L04 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: respond to and produce a short sequence of simple utterances, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: following a range of classroom instructions, for example for book-borrowing procedures and rules for using computers

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to a story and then retelling or sequencing the story using pictures

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L04-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting rhymes, songs or parts of a familiar text, including some individual performance

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L04-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a short presentation to a group on a familiar topic; for example, sharing or recounting a personal experience

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L04-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving short, simple oral presentations to the class, with supporting props; for example, presenting a ‘show and tell’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L05 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify a number of spoken text types and forms

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L05-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a variety of spoken texts such as stories, poems, plays, recounts, descriptions and instructions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L05-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using purpose, structure, content and language to help identify familiar spoken text types

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L06 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a small range of sentence forms, including common time and sequence markers to link speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common forms of statements (e.g. for those starting with ‘I am …’ and ‘This is …’) and the difference between statements and commands (e.g. between ‘She went home.’ and ‘Please give it to me.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using a variety of question stems such as ‘Who’, ‘Where’, ‘How’, ‘Why’, ‘Do you’ and ‘Can I’ (e.g. ‘Where did you live before?’) and yes/no questions (e.g. ‘Is that my book?’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common conjunctions that make connections between ideas, for example in ‘I like my dog and taking him for a walk is fun.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions that include sequence markers such as ‘first’, ‘next’, ‘and then’ and ‘after that’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L06-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using simple time markers such as ‘yesterday’, ‘later’ and ‘now’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L07 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a small range of common verb forms accurately

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing subject–verb–object sentences with accuracy, for example ‘I brushed my teeth.’ and ‘She threw the ball.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some forms of the verbs ‘to be’ and ‘to have’ correctly, for example ‘is’ in ‘Her name is Mia.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of common verb tenses for familiar verbs with some consistency; for example, using present simple tense (such as ‘walk’ and ‘go’), present continuous tense (such as ‘is walking’ and ‘is going’) and regular and common irregular past tenses (such as ‘walked’ and ‘went’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning commands with an imperative verb, for example in ‘Come over here, please.’ and ‘Bring me that book, please.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to recognise and use basic modal verbs, for example in ‘want to’, ‘have to’ and ‘should’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L07-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple negation using common auxiliary verbs such as ‘don’t’, ‘did not’ and ‘can’t’ in full and contracted forms, for example ‘The bus did not come.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L08 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a number of different phrase forms

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving some additional detail using short noun groups or adjectival phrases, for example in ‘He gave me a new book.’ and ‘I ran really fast.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding some common phrases or clauses in both their full and contracted forms, for example ‘I am’ and ‘I’m’, ‘you are’ and ‘you’re’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common prepositions such as ‘in’, ‘on’ and ‘at’ to add simple detail about place, for example in ‘Go on the train.’ and ‘Stay at home.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding instructions incorporating place or location, for example for ‘Come over here.’ and ‘Stand next to the chair.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of personal pronouns such as ‘I’, ‘me’, ‘he’, ‘him’, ‘she’, ‘they’ and ‘it’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L08-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of possessive pronouns such as ‘his’, ‘her’, ‘its’, ‘our’, ‘their’ and ‘my’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L09 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify key words and ideas from short, familiar spoken texts supported by context

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L09-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar and learnt vocabulary in short spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L09-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of words related to familiar topics; for example, using words related to family, school, shapes, numbers, days and months

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L09-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using words from lexical sets related to topics of conversation; for example, using words for favourite foods, pastimes and pets

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L10 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use pronunciation accurately, including words with consonant blends at the beginning and end, and words with more than one syllable

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: substituting middle sounds in spoken words to make new words such as ‘pin’, ‘pen’ and ‘pan’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: substituting final sounds in spoken words; for example, substituting the ‘t’ in ‘pet’ with ‘g’ to form a new word, ‘peg’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and repeating rhyming words using blends of phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words), for example ‘share’ and ‘chair’, ‘mind’ and ‘find’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: blending 2 or 3 phonemes to make syllables, for example ‘b-oo-k’ and ‘sh-ee-t’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying spoken words or syllables that contain the same phonemes, for example ‘bump’ and ‘camp’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L10-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding, substituting or deleting phonemes in any position in one-syllable words with up to 4 phonemes to generate new words

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L11 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of stress and intonation patterns to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using stress and intonation appropriately in common utterances; for example, stressing key words in short utterances and using rising intonation when asking questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing emotions such as surprise and frustration through intonation

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to sentence stress, intonation, volume and pace when rehearsing or performing role-plays

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using body language, facial expressions and gestures to enhance the meaning of speech, such as nodding and pointing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L11-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating the teacher and peers to read short texts with accurate pronunciation, fluency, pauses and intonation

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L12 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify basic differences between spoken English and home language(s)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L12-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing differences between English and home language social practices in interactions; for example, addressing people using honorifics or their name, considering formality of language used when communicating with older or younger people and using appropriate body language during interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L12-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating questions in English and a home language to clarify classroom instructions or new ideas and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L12-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording translations of unfamiliar words in a simple personal vocabulary list, including words and definitions in English and a home language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L13 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of strategies to self-assess and negotiate spoken communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L13-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating pronunciation used by the teacher and peers for a variety of interactions and text types, and repeating a sentence or phrase, modelling rhythm, intonation and pronunciation on the speech of others

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L13-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: interrupting to ask a speaker to repeat or speak slowly, for example by asking ‘Say again, please.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L13-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking help or clarification from other speakers using a home language or methods such as gesture or rewording, for example by referring to a speaker’s key words when asking for clarification: Teacher: ‘Get your diary.’ Student: ‘What is diary?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L13-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking directly what a word means; for example, saying ‘I don’t understand. What’s a “tuckshop”?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L14 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L14-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification from other home language speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L14-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L14-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking other home language speakers to translate specific words

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2L15 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and maintain simple spoken interactions with others

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating activities with peers in small-group tasks, for example by making suggestions, agreeing, disagreeing or clarifying

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding with short extended responses, including answering questions, adding to other speakers’ points and giving personal opinions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2L15-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating meaning by using gestures, modified speech, simple questions and clarifications

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R01 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the themes or main ideas of a small range of simple, familiar texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R01-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the main idea in a text, based on recognising repeated or familiar content words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R01-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading well-known words or phrases such as ‘Tuesday’ and ‘once upon a time’ in new contexts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R01-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar vocabulary in unfamiliar texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R01-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a variety of topic-related texts, including information, imaginative and persuasive texts, with support

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R02 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand information in texts read and viewed in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R02-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating understanding of simple factual or fictional texts by performing a task; for example, following written instructions to plant a seed in a pot or dramatising or illustrating parts of a story

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R02-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions or ‘true or false’ questions, sequencing information from a text, and/or matching phrases and sentences from the text to images or diagrams showing the same ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R02-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a text, for example by illustrating a section or answering questions about the text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R02-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating understanding of new texts and responding to them; for example, reading along with repeated sections or predicting what comes next

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R03 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand how different types of images in texts contribute to meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R03-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing a variety of factual and imaginative texts incorporating images such as illustrated stories, reports with diagrams, short documentaries and infographic posters

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R03-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using images to discern the storyline of a text and predict individual words in texts about familiar topics

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R03-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information from simple diagrams or graphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R03-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between images and print text, for example by matching a character’s name to an image or finding the name of a country on a map

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R04 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use knowledge of context, text structure and language to understand literal meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R04-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: employing a variety of reading cues such as images to help predict meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R04-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting what might happen next in a narrative with a familiar setting or characters

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R04-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the qualities or feelings of a character in simple terms, based on images and descriptions in print text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R04-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between the text and their own experience or other texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R05 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify differences in text genres

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R05-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing a variety of text types, including recount, report, procedure, narrative, poem, song, slide show, webpage and podcast

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R05-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering questions about text purpose and organisation, for example when asked ‘Which text tells us how to do something?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R05-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the topic and structure of a text based on its layout and visual appearance (e.g. by answering questions such as ‘Which texts use headings?’) and matching labels to specific features of a text (e.g. for author, heading, diagram and blurb)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R05-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using texts purposefully; for example, locating specific information in a known text by following links and headings, or using a simple contents page or index, for example when asked ‘Use the contents list to find the section about oceans.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R06 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise an increasing number of high-frequency words in different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching a range of familiar spoken words with print words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using initial letters and common letter patterns to decode unfamiliar words; for example, identifying rhyming words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising some common prefixes and suffixes such as ‘un-’ and ‘-er’, and how they change the meaning of words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying familiar patterns within unfamiliar words to support pronunciation and suggesting, when asked, other words that might look or sound similar, such as for ‘-ing’ in ‘sing’, ‘bring’ and ‘string’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar words and collocations such as ‘big bad wolf’ in different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R06-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using function words such as ‘the’, ‘and’, ‘as’, ‘in’ and ‘of’ to understand the relationships between ideas in a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R07 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use knowledge of letters and sounds to read an unfamiliar word or locate key words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising all letters of the alphabet in both upper-case and lower-case; for example, naming letters when spelling out unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that a letter can represent more than one sound, for example for the letter ‘u’ in ‘cut’, ‘put’ and ‘use’ and the letter ‘a’ in ‘cat’, ‘father’ and ‘any’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising sounds that can be produced by different letters, for example for the ‘s’ sound in ‘sat’ and ‘cent’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that a syllable must contain a vowel sound

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising beginning, middle and final sounds in words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R07-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising one- and 2-syllable words that are part of spoken vocabulary using knowledge of short vowels, common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs (2 letters that represent a single sound)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R08 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise that full stops and question marks separate text

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R08-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using punctuation to identify whether a sentence is a statement or a question

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R08-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: pausing appropriately at full stops when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R08-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a rising intonation when reading a question

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R09 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare English and home language print and digital texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R09-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fiction and non-fiction books in different languages

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R09-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that texts may reflect a variety of cultural beliefs, practices and views

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R09-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting ideas and experiences in texts with home language experience

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R09-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting an audience for a text, for example ‘This book was written for children.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R10 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select suitable texts for their own reading, and read, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting text suitable to read independently, based on topics of interest or recommendations from others

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: skimming parts of a text to check for familiar English content, images, size and amount of print, and layout, before making a selection

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing texts with those previously read, to predict the suitability of topic, language, length and structure

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to a picture or bilingual dictionary to check the spelling or meaning of English words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating words on classroom charts and vocabulary lists and adding to a simple personal vocabulary list to keep a record of words, including their spelling, meaning and pronunciation in English and home language(s)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R10-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing texts in a home language and/or English with family members and peers and orally retelling parts of a familiar or favourite English text to explain it to a family member or home language peer

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R11 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers or the teacher for the English translation and spelling of a home language word

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing notes in a home language about meaning and pronunciation when encountering unfamiliar words in texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary to find translations of unfamiliar words, and noting these in a home language and English

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting help from peers or school staff who speak the same home language to find the meaning of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording spelling, meaning and translations of unfamiliar words in a simple personal vocabulary list

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R11-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating from a home language to English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2R12 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to shared reading activities, including reading texts aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing actively to shared reading activities by joining group discussions about a text, listening to peers and giving brief, relevant responses to questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a text aloud in chorus or reciting familiar poems or rhymes

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E03 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: talking to peers in English and/or a home language about a favourite event or features of a story or poem (e.g. referring to fantasy elements, favourite characters, and interesting words or phrases) and giving a simple personal response to the text (e.g. ‘I enjoyed it.’ and ‘I learnt about …’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E04 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying with characters in a story by recounting an experience similar to that of the character, for example ‘That happened to me once, when …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E05 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing similarities and differences between the setting of a narrative and their own experience in English and/or a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2R12-E06 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding creatively to a text through art, drama, movement and music; for example, role-playing or drawing a picture, or taking part in a simple play or film

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALA2W01 - EAL Pathway A
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write short, simple narrative and information texts based on personal and learnt texts, and more complex texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W01-E01 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating the structure and style of familiar texts by using similar vocabulary, repetitive patterns, similar content or characters

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W01-E02 - EAL Pathway A
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying parts of a text and filling gaps with personal details or topic information; for example, filling in sections of a template following instructions from the teacher or in collaboration with peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALA2W01-E03 - EAL Pathway A
