curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level BL curriculum supports students who are beginners in English – and who have had minimal exposure to literacy in their home language(s) and little or no prior schooling (including early childhood education experiences) – as they develop basic knowledge, understanding and skills in English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students build their capacity to initiate and sustain simple conversations with their peers. They begin to learn the grammatical patterns of spoken English, and to recognise the ways that pronunciation, stress and intonation impact their clarity of expression. Through reciprocal exchanges, students develop an early awareness of the conventions of spoken English. Students participate in scaffolded and supported interactions with teachers and English-speaking peers to practise speaking English. Students interact with peers who speak their home language and can assist with translation. This supports students to make connections between their home language(s) and their developing English language skills.

Students are introduced to the English alphabet through a wide range of short print texts and picture books, and they begin to recognise common letters and letter patterns. They develop fundamental reading skills and practise strategies that assist with the decoding of simple texts. Students use visual texts to support their comprehension, including illustrations, picture dictionaries and home language–English bilingual word charts. Students participate in shared experiences with their teachers and peers to develop their reading and viewing skills, including paired reading aloud activities, small group tasks with targeted comprehension activities and classroom learning.

Students learn about the writing process. Targeted spelling and writing activities support students to develop a knowledge of some English phoneme–grapheme correspondences and the spelling of high-frequency words. Students practise writing, focusing on the formation of letters and letter placement. Through reading different texts, students begin to understand the structure and purpose of simple print texts.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level BL, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body:
Students communicate in familiar social and classroom contexts, using simple formulaic and some creative structures. They understand spoken English that is supported by teacher direction and cues from classroom context. They contribute relatively complex ideas through simple spoken English, and use simple English to respond to the ideas of others. This is achieved through continuing support and scaffolding from teachers and English-speaking peers who provide authentic interactions and space to practise English. Peers who speak home language(s) also offer shared translation opportunities. This supports students to make connections between their home language(s) and their developing English language skills.

Students use short utterances and simple subject–verb–object constructions. They use common adjectives and adverbs to describe or add emphasis. They use repeated grammar patterns copied from stories, songs, rhymes or other short texts. Students’ pronunciation, stress and intonation are comprehensible but carry elements of home language pronunciation. They use some basic communication strategies, such as asking for repetition, and by questioning to check, clarify or confirm understanding. They use some basic strategies to initiate and sustain simple conversations in English, including restating, repeating or re-pronouncing as appropriate.

modes.mode_body:
Students read a variety of short, simple, familiar, repetitive fiction and everyday texts in print and digital form, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They complete basic structured activities for the texts they read.

Students retell simple, familiar stories, and sequence a process using simple sentences and pictures. They understand that texts are written for a variety of purposes. They understand the basic phoneme–grapheme correspondences of English. Students read some familiar words and phrases in context. They recognise, name and know the sounds related to all letters and some common letter groups. They recognise that meaning is carried by intonation, and they listen for key words and for repetition of words and phrases in texts read aloud. They focus on illustrations and other non-written features when reading. They use vocabulary lists and simple pictorial and bilingual dictionaries to assist them to read unfamiliar words.

modes.mode_body:
Students communicate their ideas and experiences simply through written, drawn, copied or dictated texts. They contribute to whole-class or small-group shared writing activities. They understand that written texts in English comprise specific conventions, which change according to context and purpose. They write simple sequenced descriptions, recounts and procedures, following models. They write or draw for specific audiences. Students engage in a variety of writing activities where they develop ideas with peers, seek feedback from teachers and use model texts to inform their own writing.

Students’ writing reflects the text structures and linguistic features of their spoken language. They link ideas using common conjunctions, and understand the purpose of basic punctuation and use it in their texts. They demonstrate knowledge of some English phoneme–grapheme correspondences and spelling of high-frequency words, and show evidence of some planning. They model their writing on shared writing activities and published texts, and use some basic strategies, such as copying words or phrases from lists, using images and asking how to write a word. They begin to form letters and place text appropriately. They copy and write texts using digital tools.

elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: listen attentively, attending to intonation and body language

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some appropriate body language and gestures when listening, such as nodding and using facial expressions

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tone and intonation to distinguish between statements and questions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: respond verbally and/or non-verbally when spoken to

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding briefly, verbally or non-verbally, to simple, direct questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple, predictable personal questions on common topics such as name, age, likes and dislikes, and offering single-word responses

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: carrying out simple, familiar instructions, for example when asked ‘Please shut the door.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL02-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following simple instructions using the actions of others as cues, for example by moving to the floor or collecting a book

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL02-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating agreement or non-agreement, for example with body language, gestures such as nodding or shaking their head, or using simple utterances such as ‘yes’ and ‘no’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in highly contextualised and familiar social situations and learning activities, with significant teacher or peer support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic utterances modelled by or copied from the teacher, peers or texts to ask questions, to aid social interaction or for self-expression, for example ‘What’s the time?’, ‘Excuse me …’, ‘Oh, no!’ and ‘Very good!’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple requests or expressing needs using actions, single words and short phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple responses such as nodding or saying ‘yes’, ‘no’ or short learnt phrases

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand short verbal exchanges between speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using paralinguistic (non-verbal) responses during verbal exchanges between others; for example, nodding to indicate agreement when discussing their favourite ice-cream flavour

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding verbally using simple responses such as ‘yes’, ‘no’ or short learnt phrases to verbal exchanges between others, for example when determining the rules of a game during lunchtime

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise some familiar spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar spoken texts used frequently in class, for example in response to routine instructions such as ‘Please put your books in the tub.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between simple, familiar questions and instructions through intonation and context

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: construct 2- or 3-word utterances, with the support of actions, gestures or visuals

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common vocabulary and short formulaic expressions to communicate intention, for example ‘Please shut the door.’ and ‘Turn on the light.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing, miming or gesturing to supplement speech

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use basic verb forms in context

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple grammatical patterns such as subject plus verb (e.g. ‘We eat.’) and verb plus object (e.g. ‘Go toilet.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching simple verb tense to time words, for example ‘Yesterday we went …’ and ‘Today we go …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ‘no’ or ‘not’ with adjectives or nouns to express negative forms, for example in ‘Not hot today.’ and ‘Not me.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use common descriptive language

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common adjectives to express affect (such as ‘sad’, ‘happy’ and ‘angry’), judgement (such as ‘kind’ and ‘mean’) and appreciation (such as ‘beautiful’ and ‘yucky’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining some common adverbs with verbs to describe action, for example ‘walk slowly’ and ‘sing well’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: respond to key words in a range of familiar and common situations

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to charts or vocabulary lists to select words required for communicative needs

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using a narrow range of learnt word patterns and familiar words related to immediate needs, for example for words related to family, school, colours, numbers and days

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use comprehensible pronunciation for familiar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using accurate pronunciation for a narrow range of familiar words, including personal language, classroom language and some basic topic vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying a word when given its sounds, for example ‘lip’ for ‘l-i-p’ and ‘munch’ for ‘m-u-n-ch’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying whether sounds are the same or different, for example for the sounds in ‘ship’ and ‘sheep’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL10-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying an unfamiliar word when the beginning phoneme (the smallest unit of sound in a word), middle or end phoneme in the word is replaced with a different phoneme, for example ‘run’ to ‘fun’ and then ‘fun’ to ‘fan’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL10-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying syllables in known spoken words and names; for example, clapping the rhythm of ‘Fri-day’, ‘Jun-ko’ or ‘Shan-a-ya’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand and use basic sentence stress, intonation and paralinguistic (non-verbal) features

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between questions, instructions and statements, based on intonation and contextual information such as the actions of other students

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating the teacher’s speech when reciting or chorusing stories, songs or rhymes

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate paralinguistic (non-verbal) communication to support meaning; for example, making eye contact, nodding and gesturing

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: modifying voice features such as volume, pace, intonation and emphasis to suit different audiences and situations

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: distinguish spoken English from other languages and attempt to respond appropriately

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising when English is being spoken

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: assessing which language(s) a speaker knows and responding in that language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: repeat or re-pronounce words or phrases when prompted or if not understood, and ask for help

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a listener’s body language and speech to determine whether their own speech has been understood

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to self-correct pronunciation when a listener does not understand a word being spoken and/or repeat words using different pronunciation

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking a listener to model correct pronunciation

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: clarifying instructions before acting, for example by repeating key words (e.g. ‘The door?’) or pointing

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and using a speaker’s key words when asking for clarification, for example ‘What means “sibling”?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for help or clarification from the teacher or peers using simple formulaic expressions to make requests or ask questions, for example ‘Please say again.’ and ‘What is that?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL13-E07 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: borrowing and adapting key words from conversation partners by using techniques such as reordering; for example, Teacher: ‘Don’t be silly, Tim.’ Student: ‘Tim silly.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on home language resources to enhance learning when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers for help translating personal needs and responses from a home language to English

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification from other home language speakers

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLL15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: take turns to speak or listen during class interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a range of interactive behaviour, for example by listening, responding and turn-taking

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions in home language(s) about classroom activities and topics

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding responses from peers that combine elements of English, home language(s) and gesture

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLL15-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a narrow range of simple formulaic social expressions, for example ‘please’, ‘thank you’ and ‘May I play?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the main themes or ideas of some simple, familiar texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a familiar book or text by its topic, for example when asked ‘Which book is about the rainforest?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading classroom signs, labels or words from classroom charts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing pictures to match the order of a set of instructions or a narrative

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR01-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions about the main ideas in a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract information from short, simple texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising a friend’s name on a birthday calendar, or reading a label to select the correct book

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to name labels when speaking to peers or handing out completed work

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to simple, familiar questions or instructions read aloud by the teacher, for example when asked ‘Point to the one with a tail.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract information from simple images, with teacher direction and support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the purpose of some everyday signs around the classroom, when directed by the teacher

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching a short description to an image, for example for ‘It is green, with big eyes.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using visual clues to locate information on a map, for example for ‘the city marked with a green dot’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: make simple predictions or inferences about a text, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing a short series of pictures or simple sentences in the predicted order

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions predicting events in a familiar text, for example when asked ‘Where will they go next?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore texts in different media and modes

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that different texts, such as picture books, class writing and diaries, have different purposes

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: navigating different types of texts; for example, turning the pages of a book, swiping to turn the page of a digital book and clicking hyperlinks on a multimodal text

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying similarities and differences between written texts and digital texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand and explore the basic layout and conventions of simple texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions about the features of a text, for example when asked ‘What is the name of this text?’ and ‘Where is there a list in this text?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following step-by-step instructions to find information in a text, for example when asked ‘Open to the contents page. Now find the entry that says “Ocean”. Which page should we turn to?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that some texts have features such as contents pages, headings and images, which help readers to navigate them and make meaning

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: sequence words to make simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: putting words jumbled in a sentence from a familiar text into the correct order

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a cloze activity using the correct definite and indefinite articles, for example for ‘I saw ___ [a] star in ___ [the] sky.’ and ‘I saw ___ [the] moon last night.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating their own sentence(s), based on a given image

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple present and past tense verb forms to talk about ongoing, current and past actions

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating action verbs in a text, with teacher support; for example, using a highlighter pen to indicate action verbs in a short passage

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching the appropriate tense of action verbs to images provided either on a piece of paper or digitally

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: filling in the blanks of a column chart that has column headings ‘past’, ‘present’ and ‘future’, with some given words prefilled

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use some high-frequency adjective–noun and verb–adverb combinations

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing illustrations using short noun phrases and verb phrases; for example, saying ‘big ball’, ‘run fast’ and ‘walk slowly’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing an object in their classroom to a peer; for example, saying ‘blue chair’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR09-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a cloze activity where the noun is provided and students add an adjective or where the verb is provided and students fill in the adverb; pictures may be provided alongside written text for further support

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise some common words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and reading personally significant words, for example when seeing their own name on charts, book labels or name tags

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying common sight words and phrases from familiar charts, labels and books

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common sight words during shared reading by tracking and reading aloud with others

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise the letters and sounds of the alphabet and their basic relationships

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating specific letters, both lower-case and upper-case, in a short text or on a keyboard when prompted

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying learnt phoneme–grapheme relationships to decode vowel–consonant (VC) and consonant–vowel–consonant (CVC) words

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to pronounce unfamiliar words by using the most common sound for each letter and sounds for familiar letter groups, following instructions from the teacher, for example when asked ‘What does the first letter sound like?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising their own name, short words used regularly and consonant–vowel–consonant (CVC) words such as ‘bag’, ‘top’ and ‘get’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying common letters or letter patterns in words in letter charts, familiar books or other texts, including decodable texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR11-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that different ways of forming letters and different fonts do not change word meaning

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise spaces, capital letters and full stops when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising capital letters at the start of a sentence or a name during a shared reading experience

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that spaces are used to separate words in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spaces to count words in a sentence or on a line

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR12-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that capital letters and full stops can represent boundaries of a sentence, and using this knowledge to count sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR12-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: pausing at full stops when reading aloud

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: distinguish English from home language texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and pointing to English words in a bilingual or multilingual text

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating which books are in English and which are in their home language(s) from a small collection by sorting them into groups

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: holding an English language book with the correct orientation and turning to the correct page when given a page number

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: tracking words with a finger while listening to a simple text read aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding terms such as ‘book’, ‘author’, ‘picture’ and ‘word’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select suitable texts for their own reading, with teacher and peer support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring a new book before reading, by looking at the cover, images, amount of print and familiar elements

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with picture books selected by the teacher, and some self-selected books

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking books in their home language(s), bilingual texts and texts related to familiar topics to share with family members

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on home language resources to enhance learning when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for help with meaning from a bilingual teacher or home language peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording unfamiliar words and their meanings in a home language in a personal vocabulary list

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLR16 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in shared reading activities, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the key features of and distinguishing between fiction and non-fiction texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying familiar settings, characters or events in stories

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions about personal experience related to stories, for example when asked ‘Have you ever …?’ and ‘Do you like … too?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching words that describe emotions with images in a book such as ‘happy’ and ‘sad’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a simple personal opinion about a text, for example ‘I like it.’ or ‘It’s interesting.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating like or dislike of a character, or pointing out a favourite image or page

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E07 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to a teacher or peer read a text aloud, chorusing reading and imitating pronunciation, intonation, emphasis and key repeated phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLR16-E08 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading aloud in turns and self-correcting pronunciation if a listener does not understand the word being read aloud

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLW01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: copy words, phrases or sentences accurately and carefully

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLW01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: tracing or copying letters, words and sentences written by the teacher

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLW01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying words from everyday signs and labels, or practising tracing and writing letters, words or numbers from charts or an alphabet strip

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLW01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making corrections to their own writing when copying text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALBLW02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write some familiar words and complete simple, repetitive modelled sentences in writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALBLW02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing familiar or formulaic words and sentences to communicate information, for example ‘My name is …’

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level B1 curriculum supports students who have had some exposure to English, and to age-equivalent schooling in their home language(s) and literacy, to develop both verbal and paralinguistic (non-verbal) communication skills. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to follow simple instructions, answer predictable questions, make basic requests and express needs simply. Through active participation in conversations, students learn about the ways that English changes according to context and audience.

Students explore a wide range of familiar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. With support, they read short, familiar texts based on simple language structures and features, common vocabulary and familiar contexts. They actively participate in modelled, shared and teacher-supported independent reading and writing activities. They use simple home language–English bilingual dictionaries to check meaning or spelling. They also develop knowledge about context, phoneme–grapheme correspondences, spoken and sight vocabulary, conventions of text organisation and English grammar that assists them to read and write by engaging with peers and working closely with teachers to build confidence.

Students create and present simple texts for a variety of basic purposes. With support, they learn to communicate familiar ideas and experiences. Students engage with different texts, studying basic structures and features of these texts so that they can incorporate these into their own writing.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level B1, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body:
Students communicate verbally and non-verbally in routine and familiar social and classroom situations, supported by cues in the immediate context. They use formulas, well-rehearsed and common sentence patterns, and short, simple utterances to contribute relatively complex ideas, usually about concrete subject matter.

Students follow simple instructions, answer predictable questions, make basic requests and express their needs using simple sentences. They understand that English changes according to context and audience, and they modify their use of English in response to a range of familiar classroom and social purposes. They use appropriate social formulas and non-verbal language. Their utterances are characterised by varying grammatical accuracy. They use common adjectives and adverbs to describe or add emphasis. They use basic communication strategies, asking for repetition and questioning to clarify and confirm understanding. They restate their ideas and repeat or re-pronounce key words when necessary.

modes.mode_body:
Students read short, familiar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts, that use simple language structures and features, common vocabulary and familiar contexts. They retell simple stories, predict likely outcomes, sequence ideas and complete basic comprehension activities. 

Students understand the basic purposes of texts and choose texts appropriate for their purpose. With support, they read and gather basic information from simple, accessible texts. When reading, students combine their basic knowledge of English phoneme–grapheme correspondences, their developing spoken and sight vocabulary, their knowledge of the conventions of text organisation and their knowledge of English grammar. They use appropriate intonation and phrasing when reading aloud, showing an understanding of a text’s meaning and the function of basic punctuation. They demonstrate understanding of a narrow range of text organisational features including headings, labels, diagrams and contents pages.

modes.mode_body:
Students write and present simple texts for a variety of basic classroom and personal purposes. With support, they communicate familiar ideas, events and experiences, writing simple narratives, recounts, descriptions and reports. They use some of the basic structures and features common to these text types, demonstrating a growing awareness that purpose influences the way texts are written and presented. 

Students’ written texts incorporate the basic grammatical features of their spoken English. They spell some common and familiar words accurately and make plausible attempts to spell unfamiliar words using known English phoneme–grapheme correspondences. They use simple strategies for spelling words, such as checking vocabulary lists or books. With support, they plan and edit their texts, providing additional information through visual images. They use a range of digital tools to write and present their texts.

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping sentences about the same topic into simple paragraphs, for example ‘Frogs are green. Frogs have big eyes. They eat insects.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words to write a simple topic sentence at the beginning of most paragraphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying topic sentences or parts of sentences to support idea generation and to structure writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E05 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E06 - EAL Pathway B

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W06 - EAL Pathway B
content_descriptions.text: sequence ideas using short sentences or statements

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E01 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic time markers such as ‘On Monday …’, ‘First …’, ‘After that …’ and ‘Last …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic sentence beginnings throughout a text (e.g. ‘On the weekend, I … And then I … Then I …’) and using simple pronoun references to avoid repeating the subject in consecutive sentences (e.g. ‘Emma came to school early. She felt very tired.’ and ‘Yesterday the class went … We went …’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing basic compound sentences with a narrow range of coordinating conjunctions such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’, for example ‘I caught a bus and then walked.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing basic complex sentences using some common subordinating conjunctions such as ‘because’, ‘when’ and ‘after’, for example ‘After we finished dinner, Mum wanted to play a game.’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W07 - EAL Pathway B
content_descriptions.text: use common verb forms correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E01 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E02 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple negative constructions accurately, for example ‘I do not like …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a narrow range of adverbs and phrases to add circumstance, for example ‘The car goes fast.’ and ‘I sat on a chair.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple comparative adjectives in basic sentences with varying accuracy, for example ‘My brother bigger than me.’

elaborations.elaboration_text: matching words to definitions or labelling diagrams

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W09-E03 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.elaboration_text: forming simple noun groups that combine one or 2 adjectives with a noun, for example ‘hot day’ and ‘scary old house’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating short adverbial phrases, for example ‘on my bike’, ‘with his brother’ and ‘every week’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a variety of key words in a range of familiar and common situations

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting a small number of words from a common topic or theme, for example ‘bike’, ‘wheel’, ‘tyre’ and ‘handlebars’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar and learnt vocabulary in short spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L09-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common synonyms (such as ‘hot’ and ‘warm’) and antonyms (such as ‘fast’ and ‘slow’) to communicate a variety of meanings

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use comprehensible pronunciation for a range of high-frequency words learnt in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing comprehensible pronunciation through imitation and rehearsal

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using accurate pronunciation for a range of high-frequency words used in classroom instructions, texts and interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: substituting middle sounds in spoken words to make new words (e.g. changing ‘pin’ to ‘pen’) and substituting final sounds in spoken words (e.g. substituting the ‘t’ in ‘pet’ with ‘g’ to form a new word, ‘peg’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and repeating rhyming words using blends of phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words), for example for ‘share’ and ‘chair’, ‘mind’ and ‘find’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and producing phonemes in blends or clusters at the beginning and end of syllables, for example in ‘sh-ip’ and ‘di-sh’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L10-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: blending 2 or 3 phonemes together to make syllables, for example in ‘b-oo-k’ and ‘sh-ee-t’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use sentence stress, intonation and other paralinguistic (non-verbal) features to support communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to and using intonation and tone to distinguish between questions, instructions and statements

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and imitating features of sounds and intonation in the speech of the teacher and peers, and in video or audio clips

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing emotions such as happiness and anger through intonation

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate paralinguistic (non-verbal) features to support meaning; for example, making eye contact and using facial expressions, gestures and posture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify differences between aspects of spoken English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the sounds and words of English in interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking the teacher or peers about appropriate behaviour in certain situations, for example ‘Should I use eye contact?’ and ‘Is it okay to shake hands?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the nature of social interactions with familiar people and in known settings; for example, learning how to greet a peer, a classroom teacher and the principal and comparing it to a home language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: ask for repetition or clarification to confirm understanding of spoken communication and ask for help

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: assessing engagement and understanding of a listener, including checking for attentive posture or confused facial expressions, noticing from the listener’s body language that something has not been understood and then repeating words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: self-correcting pronunciation or rephrasing sentences in simple ways when a listener indicates they have not understood

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: clarifying instructions before acting, by recasting key words (e.g. ‘Open them?’ and ‘These pencils?’) or by indicating the objects

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for repetition or clarification from a speaker (such as using ‘Please repeat.’ and ‘What means …?’), referring to the speaker’s key words; for example, Teacher: ‘Please get your dictionary.’ Student: ‘What is dictionary?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: checking understanding of classroom English with other home language speakers

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources to enhance learning when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating questions in English and a home language to clarify classroom instructions or new ideas and vocabulary

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1L15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: listen and speak appropriately during small-group interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: displaying appropriate listening behaviours; for example, having attentive posture and using appropriate facial expressions and gestures

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking turns attending to the expressions of other speakers, and incorporating cues such as questions or key words into their own responses

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1L15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating questions in English and a home language to clarify classroom instructions or new ideas and vocabulary

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use key words to understand the main idea in a range of simple short texts based on predictable language structures and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the main topic of a short paragraph; for example, saying ‘This is about dogs.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the main characters and events in a short narrative when given a prompt, for example when asked ‘In this paragraph, can you find the name of the main character?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract some information from simple short texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions, for example to plant a seed in a pot or draw parts of a story

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions related to labelled items or locations, for example when asked ‘Take out your laptop.’ and ‘Place your printed work in the “finished” basket.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract some information from a narrow range of images, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating city or country names on a simple map

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching phrases and sentences from a text to images or diagrams that show the same ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the topic and structure of a text based on its layout and visual appearance; for example, using headings or illustrations

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R03-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using organisational features to navigate a text, including multimodal and interactive texts; for example, using titles and headings in a print text or hyperlinks and navigational items in a digital text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: make simple predictions or inferences about a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pictures to predict the events in a narrative, or images, diagrams, graphs and tables to predict the content of an information text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting what might happen next in a narrative with a familiar setting or characters

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions based on images, for example in response to ‘How is the character feeling?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare text types and identify differences between them

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and describing a variety of text types such as recount, report, narrative, slide show, webpage and podcast

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering questions about text purpose and organisation, for example when asked ‘Which text tells us how to do something?’ and ‘Which texts use headings?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting an audience for a text, for example ‘This book is written for children.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the purpose and basic organisational features of simple text types

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using language, layout or topic to distinguish between information and fictional texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding information in a text, for example when asked ‘Use the contents list to find the section about lions.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the sequence of key words, phrases or ideas in a familiar text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a simple storyboard to show the sequence of ideas from a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: filling in missing items in a sequence of key words, phrases or sections from a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read sentences that use basic subject, verb and object patterns, where content and vocabulary are familiar

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: ordering words jumbled in a sentence to create a grammatical and logical sentence

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering literal questions about familiar texts; for example, Teacher: ‘What did the dog eat?’ Student: ‘The dog ate the bone.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify simple present and past tense verbs

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating verbs in a text and distinguishing between their tenses

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching pairs of simple present and past tense verbs such as ‘go’ and ‘went’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R09-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familiar irregular verbs such as ‘swim’ and ‘swam’ within their text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read some familiar words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using previous knowledge to read familiar sight words and phrases in unfamiliar texts, for example for words from a high-frequency word list and familiar sentence starters such as ‘Once upon a time …’ and ‘Today is …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to read new forms of familiar words, and self-correcting using knowledge of base words and common morphemes (meaningful units within words), for example for ‘walk’, ‘walked’ and ‘walks’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using initial letters and common letter patterns to decode unfamiliar words; for example, identifying rhyming words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R10-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising some common prefixes and suffixes such as ‘un-’ and ‘-er’ and how they change the meaning of words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R10-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar words and collocations such as ‘big bad wolf’ in different contexts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify common syllables and patterns within words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming letters and giving their sounds when spelling or sounding out unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising sounds that can be produced by different letters such as the ‘s’ sound in ‘sat’ and ‘cent’, and using this knowledge to decode words when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that a syllable must contain a vowel sound

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising beginning, middle and final sounds in words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising one- and 2-syllable words that are part of spoken vocabulary, using knowledge of short vowels, common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R11-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading aloud words that are familiar or contain familiar letter patterns with some accuracy and confidence

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the function of spaces, capital letters and full stops

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: pausing at a full stop when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising when words require capital letters, for example for names and at the beginning of sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why a word starts with a capital letter; for example, saying it is a name or it is the first word in a sentence

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise key differences between texts in English and in other languages

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting ways of beginning or ending a story in different languages, for example ‘Instead of “Once upon a time”, in my language we say …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with texts about ideas and events from different places, times and cultures

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in cultural features of texts in English and in a home language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select suitable books to read, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing a variety of texts with different settings and themes

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: skimming part of a book before selecting, to check for familiar English content, images, size and amount of print, and layout

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing books with those previously read to predict the suitability of topic, language, length and structure

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R14-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: re-reading familiar texts to increase accuracy and fluency, and to enhance understanding

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R14-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading texts in English and/or a home language to caregivers or siblings

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources to enhance learning when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing notes in a home language about meaning and pronunciation when encountering unfamiliar words in texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary to find translations of unfamiliar words, and noting these in a home language and English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R15-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers or the teacher for the English translation and spelling of a home language word

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1R16 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in teacher-led shared reading activities, relating aspects of imaginative texts to their own experience

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming and describing characters from a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a simple personal response to a text, for example ‘I enjoyed it.’ or ‘I learnt about …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the feelings of a character in simple terms, based on print text and accompanying images

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recounting a similar experience to that of a character (e.g. ‘That happened to me once, when …’) and describing similarities and differences between a text and their own experience (e.g. identifying events that are familiar or new)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: joining group discussions by listening to other students and giving brief, relevant responses to questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1R16-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: self-correcting pronunciation, or repeating a sentence with corrected pronunciation and improved fluency, when reading aloud

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write ‘real world’ personal texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a list of items to take on an excursion, using the names of familiar objects

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a letter introducing themselves, using some formulaic expressions such as ‘Dear …’ and ‘I live in …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a simple story to share with the class, based on listening to a story told at home

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write simple information texts for a variety of classroom purposes, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple information texts to give information or instructions, or to keep records (e.g. keeping a digital class journal)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a list of class expectations and routines

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using examples of digital ‘listicles’ as models to create their own versions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write simple imaginative texts modelled on familiar forms and repetitive patterns, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following the structure of modelled texts; for example, writing in first person, as a sequence of events or a reflection in a diary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing imaginative texts adapted from or in response to classroom texts; for example, writing a story with an alternative setting or ending

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to produce simple imaginative texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use images to support simple narrative or recount sentences, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating illustrations or diagrams to accompany sentences in a narrative or recount

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling simple diagrams or pictures using familiar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple phrases as captions or explanations for drawings

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W04-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital storyboarding to create a simple story map to show the events and characters in a narrative

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: organise some subject matter and attempt to write paragraphs and topic sentences, using modelled forms and repetitive patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using templates or graphic organisers or following model texts for organisational structure; for example, including an introduction, body paragraphs and conclusion

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping sentences about the same topic into simple paragraphs, for example ‘Frogs are green. Frogs have big eyes. They eat insects.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words to write a simple topic sentence at the beginning of most paragraphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying topic sentences or parts of sentences to support idea generation and to structure writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: separating ideas in texts by leaving a line or writing a heading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W05-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tools to format a digital text; for example, making headings using a larger font, formatting text and placing images near relevant text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: sequence ideas using short sentences or statements

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a series of short statements in time sequence, for example ‘I eat breakfast. I go to school. I read a book.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic time markers such as ‘On Monday …’, ‘First …’, ‘After that …’ and ‘Last …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic sentence beginnings throughout a text (e.g. ‘On the weekend, I … And then I … Then I …’) and using simple pronoun references to avoid repeating the subject in consecutive sentences (e.g. ‘Emma came to school early. She felt very tired.’ and ‘Yesterday the class went … We went …’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing basic compound sentences with a narrow range of coordinating conjunctions such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’, for example ‘I caught a bus and then walked.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W06-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing basic complex sentences using some common subordinating conjunctions such as ‘because’, ‘when’ and ‘after’, for example ‘After we finished dinner, Mum wanted to play a game.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use common verb forms correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common simple past tense forms with the suffix ‘-ed’ consistently, although overgeneralising rules for some less common irregular past tense verbs (e.g. writing ‘catched’, ‘freezed’ and ‘waked’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common irregular past tense verbs such as ‘went’, ‘said’ and ‘bought’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple negative constructions accurately, for example ‘I do not like …’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB1W08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a narrow range of simple descriptive phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB1W08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: building simple noun phrases using adjectives, for example ‘the blue car’

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level B2 curriculum supports students who have already had 1 to 2 years of age-appropriate formal instruction in the basics of English language and literacy, and some exposure to home language literacy learning, to develop their knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to their spoken English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to negotiate simple exchanges in English, combining their understanding of both verbal language and paralinguistic communication. They refine and further develop a wide range of fundamental communication skills in increasingly complex and de-contextualised situations and settings. They continue to learn about ways to improve consistency and fluency when speaking in English.

Students explore a wide range of familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They learn to apply their developing vocabulary and their knowledge of sentence structure and English phoneme–grapheme correspondences to predict and self-correct as they read. They use home language–English bilingual dictionaries to find specific key words. Students begin to read more widely, assessing text difficulty and selecting new texts to read with increasing independence. They participate in modelled, shared and independent reading activities, working closely with their teachers and peers who support reading aloud, encourage self-correction and model reading strategies.

Students write for a broad range of purposes on familiar topics. Students’ written texts may include a narrow range of language features, including simple and compound sentences, some unfamiliar vocabulary and some high-frequency words. They learn to plan, draft, revise and edit their writing so that they can create texts that are more detailed and sequential. Students participate in shared and independent writing activities with teacher and peer support.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level B2, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body:
Students communicate in English in predictable social and learning situations. They understand some de-contextualised English and express simple messages in basic English. They negotiate simple transactions and ask and answer simple questions on familiar topics, using familiar response structures.

Students identify and describe people, places and things using simple vocabulary. They describe a series of events or actions using some detail. They initiate and manage interactions appropriately in a range of familiar contexts. They understand instructions, recounts and explanations when contextually supported. They use simple English with varying degrees of grammatical accuracy. They combine known formulaic responses, learnt grammatical features and new vocabulary to construct new utterances. They use basic time and sequence markers, and simple negative forms. They use verb endings with some consistency. They use some of the terminology of new topics in their utterances. They pronounce familiar words comprehensibly. They employ familiar strategies to sustain and enhance communication in English.

modes.mode_body:
Students read familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts, that contain predictable structures and familiar vocabulary. 

Students follow simple written instructions and respond to simple written questions. They identify the main purposes of a range of texts and recognise the basic features of common text types. They use their developing vocabulary and their knowledge of sentence structure and English phoneme–grapheme correspondences to predict and self-correct. They modify intonation to distinguish questions, exclamations and dialogue when reading aloud. They follow logical relationships between events and ideas expressed by common cohesive devices. They sequence sentences from known texts or a text on a familiar topic or experience. They use simple strategies to assess text difficulty and to choose new texts to read.

modes.mode_body:
Students write for a range of purposes on familiar topics. They write simple, organised texts that demonstrate the use of specific vocabulary and simple sentence structures. Their writing demonstrates their understanding of the purposes, structures and features of common text types. 

Students’ written texts include basic information and simple detail. Students use common conjunctions to link ideas, and use pronoun references with some noun–pronoun agreement. They use simple phrases to express basic comparisons, and use some basic punctuation with consistency. They make plausible attempts to spell unfamiliar words using known English phoneme–grapheme correspondences. They use a range of strategies for spelling words, including checking vocabulary lists and keeping a personal dictionary. They write new sentences using known sentence structures. They draw on their knowledge of the writing process to plan and write simple texts and, with support, redraft them. They use a range of digital tools to write, edit and present their texts.

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W07-E03 - EAL Pathway B

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W08-E02 - EAL Pathway B

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L01 - EAL Pathway B
