elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and observing others to understand the nature of familiar social interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing ideas and information to extend the conversation and make connections to other speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions for clarification or elaboration of ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L01-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving personal opinions; for example, agreeing or disagreeing with a point

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify key points of information in short spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising key topic words from classroom activities and in spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recalling the sequence of ideas in a spoken text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering questions on a familiar topic using a familiar structure

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and maintain short, structured social and classroom language interactions in most familiar contexts, using conversation partners to support understanding

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple questions on familiar topics or themes and responding appropriately using support from conversation partners, for example by using gestures, modified speech and allowing a pause before responding

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using common classroom action verbs such as ‘sit’, ‘collect’, ‘open’ and ‘stop’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following a short sequence of classroom task–related instructions with clear steps and modelling of the task

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L03-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting common classroom and playground language to a narrow range of relevant situations, for example ‘Wait a minute.’, ‘Be quiet, please.’ and ‘My turn.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: role-play and retell a simple story, such as a recount, legend or fairytale, or ‘show and tell’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning the content and sequence of a story through storytelling, reading or viewing in a home language or English, and retelling in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conventions of story texts such as ‘Once upon a time …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling pronunciation, intonation and emphasis to contribute to engaging storytelling

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use the basic features of a spoken text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: modifying speech for different audiences; for example, greeting a teacher differently than a friend, or asking to borrow a book from the library, the teacher or a friend

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and producing short texts for different purposes, for example for simple recounts, descriptions and instructions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying basic text structures such as introduction, body and conclusion

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use specific time and sequence markers in speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using time markers such as ‘yesterday’, ‘last week’ and ‘on the weekend’ to indicate specific moments in the past, present and future

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using simple sequence markers such as ‘first’, ‘next’ and ‘and then’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of verb forms with increasing accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: maintaining consistency of verb tenses such as ‘-ing’ and ‘-ed’ in extended speech or conversation

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using forms of ‘to be’ or ‘to have’ as auxiliaries in common verb phrases, for example ‘It was broken.’, ‘I am eating.’ and ‘They have finished.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using auxiliary verbs to express negative forms, for example in ‘I don’t go.’ and ‘I couldn’t see.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L07-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple modal verb forms such as ‘could’, ‘might’, ‘will’, ‘must’ and ‘perhaps’ when listening to others

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L07-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use modality through verbs (e.g. in ‘It might rain.’ and ‘You can do it.’) and adverbs (e.g. in ‘Perhaps I will go.’ and ‘This is really tasty.’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple descriptive phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: building simple noun phrases to describe specific people, places and things, for example in ‘I have a very old red BMX bike.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of adverbial phrases to express circumstances of place (e.g. ‘over there’), location (e.g. ‘in the room’) and time (e.g. ‘last week’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of regular comparative adjectives (such as ‘bigger’, ‘older’ and ‘healthier’), some irregular comparatives (such as ‘better’ and ‘more’) and comparatives with words of 3 or more syllables (such as ‘more expensive’ and ‘more beautiful’), with occasional errors

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L08-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming some negative comparisons using a range of forms with developing accuracy, for example ‘not as big as’, ‘less expensive than’ and ‘less healthy than’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a narrow range of descriptive vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using descriptive vocabulary to communicate detail about specific people, places and things, including colour, size, place, location and time, for example ‘the big red book’ and ‘a park near my house’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use clear pronunciation for common words and learnt key topic words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to pronunciation and making adjustments based on the reaction of listeners or direct feedback

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using accurate pronunciation for common words and learnt words used in interpersonal interactions, classroom situations and content learning

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: blending and segmenting words into phonemes (the smallest units of sounds in words), for example ‘b-r-o-th-er’ and ‘c-l-ou-d-y’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L10-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: deleting and substituting phonemes to form new words (e.g. deleting the initial ‘scr’ in ‘scratch’ and substituting new initial sounds to form words such as ‘catch’, ‘batch’ and ‘hatch’) and substituting a middle sound to form a new word (e.g. changing ‘stack’ to ‘stick’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of sentence stress, intonation and paralinguistic (non-verbal) features to support communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising rhythm and intonation by repeating words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating features of the speech of others, including the teacher, peers, and speakers in video or audio clips

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: modifying their own intonation, volume and stress according to context and purpose; for example, shouting a warning or talking softly in group or play activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using purposeful paralinguistic (non-verbal) strategies to support meaning and engage listeners; for example, making eye contact and using facial expressions, gestures and posture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify similarities and differences between spoken English and home language(s)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying different aspects of a home language and English, for example in pronunciation and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing differences between a home language and English with home language peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating a range of simple expressions to ask the meaning of a word or phrase, for example ‘What you mean?’, ‘What means “festival”?’ and ‘What “dog”?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification, for example ‘Is this right?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring differences in simple conversation openers, turn-taking, leave-taking and social formulas, for example ‘Excuse me …’, ‘Can you please …?’ and ‘Thank you.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L12-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning how to adapt social expressions to suit the conversation partner; for example, saying ‘hi’ to a friend and ‘good morning’ to a teacher

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: self-correct and improve aspects of spoken English language use that impede communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: assessing a listener’s understanding based on body language, facial expressions and direct feedback, and attempting to self-correct pronunciation and grammar

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple formulaic expressions to ask a speaker to repeat or speak slowly, for example ‘Please say that again.’ and ‘Please say it slowly.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying specific words in a text that may pose pronunciation problems, based on guidance from the teacher, for example when asked ‘Find all the words ending in “s”.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for support with communication, for example ‘What is the difference between “walk” and “work”?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking assistance from speech partners to pronounce words or rephrase sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L13-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing and repeating memorable new terms such as the names of ingredients in a recipe or rhyming words from a poem, and incorporating new vocabulary from written texts into conversations and presentations

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing home language or bilingual resources such as dictionaries, online translation tools and information texts, to support understanding of content

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording words and information in a personal vocabulary list in both a home language and English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2L15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to small-group work and collaborative learning

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in interactions by listening actively, responding to others and contributing information and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating meaning by using gestures, modified speech, simple questions and clarifications

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2L15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying conventions of interaction such as conversational formulas, turn-taking, affirming, suggesting and discussing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify the main idea in short, simple texts, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key words in questions and finding them in a text using guide questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key words from headings or topic sentences to extract key information from an information text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract key information from a range of texts, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following simple print or digital instructions such as ‘Fill the …’, ‘Measure the …’ and ‘Record the …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple print or digital questions such as ‘How many …?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract key information from different types of images in text, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating a cell on a table, using row and column headings

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using diagrams, graphs or pictures to help interpret meaning in a written text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing written descriptions to match a series of diagrams

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: make and substantiate predictions and inferences when reading or viewing a text, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between a text and their own experience or other texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching images or names of emotions to characters and events in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of sentence structure to predict words or self-correct

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify informative, imaginative and persuasive texts when reading texts or listening to texts read aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fiction and non-fiction books by looking at the covers, titles and images

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying, sequencing and labelling structural elements of a text such as sections, headings and images

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching labels to parts of a text, for example for ‘introduction’, ‘topic sentence’ and ‘example’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R05-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying characteristics of the language of a text, for example in use of personal or technical language

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R05-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sorting and sequencing 2 texts jumbled together, for example for a story about the big bad wolf and an information report about wolves

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the purpose and organisational features of common text types

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching sections of a text with labels for their name and purpose

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making predictions about the subject matter of a text based on features such as illustrations, headings and layout

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: navigating a digital text by using a series of hyperlinks to locate specific information

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R06-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple comparisons between text types; for example, comparing the visual layout of an information report and the visual layout of a news story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the relationships between events or ideas in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sorting sentences into sets related to the same topic, and writing a heading for each set

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: arranging parts of a sentence that use cohesive devices such as ‘after that’ and ‘because’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the items that pronouns refer to, for example in ‘The dogs … They …’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read texts that contain compound and complex sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a narrow range of information and fictional texts that include compound and complex sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common coordinating conjunctions (such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’) and subordinating conjunctions (such as ‘because’, ‘if’ and ‘before’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use knowledge of simple tense and negation to interpret the meaning of written text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the base word and interpreting the effect of tense and negation, for example in ‘did not eat’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching sets of words and phrases to show their relationship, for example for the set ‘go’, ‘went’ and ‘did not go’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read some common words or familiar phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using previous knowledge to read familiar words or phrases in new texts, for example for ‘next to the’ and ‘she said’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences to read unfamiliar words, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences and familiar phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words) to make predictions about unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: breaking words into syllables and phonemes to read unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of less common sounds and words with similar letter patterns to alter pronunciation when reading aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading words with digraphs where one letter is not pronounced (such as ‘knife’ and ‘thumb’) and using them in writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading words with vowel digraphs such as ‘ee’, ‘oo’, ‘ai’, ‘ay’ and ‘ea’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R11-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using context to read the correct word when an unfamiliar word has more than one plausible pronunciation

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand simple punctuation when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sentence punctuation to identify the nature of a sentence; for example, identifying whether a sentence is a statement or a question

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using punctuation to identify parts of a sentence; for example, pausing appropriately at full stops and commas

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate pauses and emphasis when reading direct speech or dialogue aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R12-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising a question in a text and adjusting intonation appropriately when reading aloud

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare texts and aspects of texts across languages and cultures to identify similarities and differences

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a variety of texts that reflect a range of cultures and contexts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting texts with a variety of settings and characters, including those related to personal experience and those that are unfamiliar

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing ideas in texts to personal experience, for example ‘My family also cooks like this.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing personal opinion about cultural ideas in texts, for example ‘I would like to try this one day.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select and read a range of unfamiliar texts, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting a narrow range of books to read, for example with a variety of genres, topics, settings or perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the content, images, amount of print and difficulty of language of different books before selecting one to read

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading an unfamiliar text with occasional prompts and corrections from the teacher

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading word-by-word and clarifying, if the meaning breaks down, by pausing, re-reading and/or reading further

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking assistance from peers to pronounce unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R14-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a simple English dictionary or classroom vocabulary list to find words, and/or checking a bilingual dictionary for meanings

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to vocabulary lists or charts to find specific vocabulary related to a topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital resources such as digital translators or online discussions to support reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary to find an English equivalent of a word known in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: checking meaning in both a home language and English before using the word in speech or writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R15-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording words and information in a personal vocabulary list in both a home language and English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2R16 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to shared reading activities, including personal responses to an imaginative text or elements of a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a personal point of view about a character’s actions, such as indicating agreement or disagreement with a character’s actions, and giving a reason

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing their own experiences to those represented in texts, and/or making simple connections between an element of the text and personal experience; for example, suggesting their own feelings and actions in a similar situation

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections to different experiences or recounting related personal experiences, for example ‘When I …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining text-related knowledge that has been learnt previously, in a different setting

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to group discussion, contributing relevant ideas and negotiating responses to a group activity

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2R16-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating shared responses to a text; for example, answering questions or jointly writing a short extension to a story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write simple personal texts that present a point of view

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following a template or model text and filling in details to write personal texts such as letters of invitation, thanks to visitors, blogs and emails

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple texts related to personal experiences or shared classroom activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a statement of opinion with a simple structure, including the opinion and reasons

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W01-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing to express likes or dislikes related to a class topic, or agreement or disagreement with an issue discussed in class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write simple information texts based on model texts provided or studied in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a narrow range of information texts, such as reports, procedures, captions for images and explanations, using example texts to guide construction

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: including some features of text types; for example, using an introduction, list of requirements, or steps beginning with a verb in a procedure

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing information texts by hand or using digital tools, using the structure and language features of a model text as a reference

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W02-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding captions for images when composing information texts, using examples from model texts as a reference

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write imaginative texts based on model texts provided or studied in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using language features of model texts, such as the rhyme and metre of poems, to compose their own creative texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following conventions of texts based on classroom models, for example for character names and stage directions in a script

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating personal experience, ideas adapted from other texts or imaginative details into creative texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: add visual information to written texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating a narrative to reflect descriptions in a written text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding a copied diagram to a digital information report, with features and key words that are used in the written text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating diagrams or tables close to relevant information in print and digital texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W04-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using text layout tools in a computer app when creating digital texts; for example, aligning or resizing images

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W04-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a storyboard with images in sequence and text written underneath them

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use headings and paragraphs appropriate to the task

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using headings and subheadings to group information in a report; for example, including ‘Description’, ‘Habitat’ and ‘Diet’ in a report on an animal

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: separating sections in texts by starting a new idea on a new line, or a new section on a new page

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping sentences about the same topic into a paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W05-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising sentences using a simple sequence, for example by using chronological order of events or strong to weak arguments

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W05-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words to write a simple topic sentence that states the main idea of a paragraph

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple connectives and pronoun references to connect ideas in a sentence

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple time sequence markers such as ‘first’, ‘next’ and ‘at last’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of pronoun references to connect ideas in text, including ‘he’, ‘she’, ‘it’, ‘we’, ‘they’, ‘his’, ‘her’ and ‘their’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing compound sentences with an expanding range of coordinating conjunctions (such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’), for example ‘I caught the train and then walked to the beach but I didn’t go swimming.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W06-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing complex sentences using some common subordinating conjunctions (such as ‘because’, ‘if’ and ‘when’), for example ‘When Sam opened the door, her puppy ran to greet her.’ and ‘He can’t drink milk because he is allergic.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of verb forms correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: maintaining consistency of verb tenses by using the correct word endings (such as ‘-ing’ and ‘-ed’) in a paragraph or short text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ‘to be’ as an auxiliary verb in common phrases, for example in simple passive constructions (e.g. ‘It was broken.’) or continuous tenses (e.g. in ‘I am eating.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the auxiliary verb form of ‘to have’ in common phrases, for example in ‘They have finished.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W07-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a narrow range of complex negatives with some accuracy, for example with appropriate subject–verb agreement (e.g. in ‘He doesn’t like.’) or modality (e.g. in ‘She can’t come.’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB2W08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple extended descriptive phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB2W08-E01 - EAL Pathway B

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level B3 curriculum supports students who have already had 2 to 3 years of age-appropriate formal instruction in the basics of English language and literacy, and some exposure to home language literacy, to enhance their knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to their spoken English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to respond to and use English appropriately in a wide range of contexts. Pronunciation, stress and intonation are the focus for extending students’ spoken skills. Students learn strategies to self-correct and adapt language to convey meaning more clearly.

Students explore a wide range of familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They learn to identify the main ideas in texts, and to paraphrase their understanding in spoken English. They develop strategies that help them to read unfamiliar texts, including using bilingual dictionaries to build vocabulary knowledge. Students expand their known repertoire of written text types. They apply their understanding of purpose and audience to shape their writing. They explore how to sequence paragraphs by using conjunctions, and how to create consistent tenses to help clarify expression. They plan, draft, revise and edit their writing to improve spelling, punctuation and sentence structure. They learn strategies such as referring to a bilingual dictionary to confirm accuracy of spelling and word choice. Through a range of shared and independent writing activities, students incorporate feedback into their written texts.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level B3, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students appropriately respond to and use the structures and features of spoken English in a variety of familiar formal and informal contexts. They demonstrate awareness of the register requirements such as tone, formality of language, vocabulary and body language of spoken English that are used when speaking for different purposes. They understand the essential meaning of unfamiliar topics expressed in familiar spoken English, and extract specific information from spoken texts. They use appropriate sequence markers and consistently use the most common irregular past tenses. They provide detail by using longer noun groups and adverbial phrases when speaking, and use comprehensible pronunciation, stress and intonation. They access English from a variety of spoken and written sources, and extend their spoken skills by incorporating new vocabulary from these sources into their own repertoire. They self-correct some errors, reformulate language to convey meaning more clearly, and add essential details.

modes.mode_body: Students read with increasing independence for a range of purposes, and identify the main ideas and specific information in classroom texts. These texts may be print or digital, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. Students demonstrate understanding of the main storyline and most key information when retelling, paraphrasing and answering questions, and they compare details in texts. They demonstrate awareness of how information is organised in English texts. They recognise the cohesive devices that connect ideas and the organisation of information in a text. They use appropriate metalanguage to talk about the structure and features of a text. They recognise how relationships are signalled by an increasing range of conjunctions. They integrate a number of strategies to help them read unfamiliar texts. They use English dictionaries to check the meaning of unfamiliar words, and use contents pages, indexes, glossaries and headings to find information.

modes.mode_body:
Students communicate for a range of purposes on a variety of topics, using a repertoire of familiar text types. They write sequenced and ordered information texts, and narrative texts that maintain a cohesive storyline and characterisation. They demonstrate an awareness of how effective writing is tailored to a purpose, the requirements of the topic and the needs of the reader. They gather and present information appropriately in texts. They write texts that demonstrate overall cohesion and coherence.

Students can combine and sequence simple sentences and paragraphs using common conjunctions and pronouns. They generally maintain appropriate tense throughout their texts. They discuss and reflect on their own writing, incorporating feedback when planning, reviewing or presenting their texts. They revise texts during writing, and proofread them after a first draft has been written, improving spelling, punctuation and sentence structure. They present their writing appropriately, in print and digital forms.

substrand_content_descriptions.text: present a simple prepared talk on a familiar topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: replicating features of a selected situation; for example, using interpersonal language in a negotiation or formal expression in a talk

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising and improving pronunciation, phrasing, fluency, intonation, volume and pace when rehearsing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify and use features of formal and informal spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and following the structure of formal spoken texts; for example, introducing, giving a message and concluding

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a style of speech appropriate to its purpose such as to inform, to persuade or to entertain

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use appropriate sequence markers

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding sequence markers in spoken texts, such as ‘first’, ‘second’ and ‘finally’, and using these to order written text or pictures

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: structuring their own spoken texts using a variety of sequence markers, such as ‘first’, ‘finally’, ‘until’ and ‘when’, for example in recounts, procedures and explanations

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use complex verb forms with increasing accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying verb tenses more consistently; for example, using most common irregular past tenses such as in ‘came’, ‘gave’, ‘thought’ and ‘said’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using correct subject–verb agreement with simple and some complex tenses, for example in ‘I go’, ‘she goes’ and ‘My cousin has come to visit.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising modal verbs that express probability and possibility, for example for ‘may’, ‘will’, ‘could’ and ‘must’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding modality when listening to others, and responding appropriately, for example in response to ‘You may pack up, but you must stay inside.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modal verbs to express a point of view, for example ‘I will enjoy that.’ and ‘It could fall over.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L07-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming multi-word negatives accurately; for example, including auxiliary and modal verbs (such as in ‘He did not need to carry that.’) and expressing a more complex tense (such as in ‘She has not started yet.’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use longer descriptive phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming noun groups that incorporate a variety of elements, for example ‘frightening old haunted house’ and ‘very long, hot week’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using qualifiers in comparisons, for example in ‘She is a lot taller than her friend.’ and ‘It is not quite as hot as yesterday.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming negative comparisons accurately, for example ‘less healthy than’ and ‘not as expensive as’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L08-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of adverbial phrases to give detail about place (e.g. ‘under a shady tree’), time (e.g. ‘for a long time’), accompaniment (e.g. ‘with her best friend’) and manner (e.g. ‘in a graceful way’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of vocabulary to convey nuance

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between key words used in instructions, for example between names of classroom items such as ‘workbook’ and ‘textbook’, and between action verbs such as ‘stir’ and ‘fold’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of vocabulary to convey shades of meaning in conversations or presentations, for example ‘good’, ‘fine’, ‘terrific’ and ‘excellent’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use accurate pronunciation for all known words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to accurate pronunciation when speaking in classroom situations

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising unstressed vowels in multisyllabic words such as ‘builder’ and ‘animal’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use vocabulary, intonation, volume, stress and suprasegmental features (pacing cues) and paralinguistic features (non-verbal cues) to convey meaning and enhance communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words rather than intonation to indicate a question, for example ‘Do you …?’, ‘What is …?’ and ‘Can anybody …?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling intonation, volume, stress and pacing on the speech of others such as the teacher, peers, performers and presenters

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to the body language, facial expressions and speech of listeners to determine whether meaning has been understood

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L11-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting features of speech to support and convey meaning; for example, modifying mood in storytelling or giving emphasis when recounting news

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: talk about cultural differences in spoken language use across language and cultures

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and observing situations to understand how languages change to suit purpose, audience and topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating appropriate ways of expressing a message to suit the situation; for example, using formal or informal expression, or technical or everyday vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L12-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: speaking appropriately for the situation by modifying voice, body language and expression to match those of other speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L12-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking about appropriate paralinguistic (non-verbal) behaviours in certain situations, for example ‘Should I give eye contact?’ and ‘Is it okay to shake hands?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L12-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with home language peers to clarify new vocabulary and ideas

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: self-evaluate and improve aspects of spoken English language use to enhance communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to the responses of listeners to judge whether clarification is needed, for example by using body language, facial expressions and verbal feedback

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: clarifying and/or elaborating on meaning, for example ‘I mean …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying patterns of pronunciation that pose difficulty in their own speech, for example in articulating final consonants or a specific vowel sound and in using inappropriate word stress

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing pronunciation with a partner or recording pronunciation using a digital device for self-assessment, in order to make improvements

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing errors in pronunciation, vocabulary choice and grammar, and attempting to correct these

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L13-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking assistance or feedback from speech partners to formulate or confirm corrected expressions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on an extensive range of home language resources when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification from other home language speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to a home language or bilingual texts such as glossaries, dictionaries and online translation tools for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L14-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording words and information in a personal dictionary or notes, using a combination of English and a home language to indicate meaning, pronunciation and usage

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3L15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and manage interaction in collaborative group work

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and managing interaction in a range of collaborative group-work situations; for example, during class discussions, small-group brainstorming and pair activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting appropriately for a situation, for example by formulating a structured response in a class discussion or negotiating meaning in a small-group activity

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening and responding to other speakers appropriately; for example, acknowledging, clarifying or building on what they say when participating in brainstorming

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3L15-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing information that elaborates or clarifies a topic, or expressing ideas or opinions in response to other speakers

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify and compare the main ideas in a variety of texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions to find the appropriate page in a book, and identifying the topic and main ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding answers to simple questions such as ‘Where did …?’ and ‘Who was the …?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R01-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding and comparing 2 simple websites on the same topic to choose the more appropriate one

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R01-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: retelling a story through speech or writing, including giving characters and settings, and sequencing key events correctly

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract detailed information from a variety of texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: skimming and scanning a text to identify the topic, and extracting specific details

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the ingredients section in a simple recipe to ascertain the correct amount of each ingredient

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R02-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: assembling familiar equipment in the correct arrangement to conduct a simple science experiment

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R03 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret and explain information from a range of images in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R03-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: following menus or hyperlinks to navigate a website, and using digital icons for common functions such as searching, downloading and printing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R03-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting data points on a bar graph; for example, identifying the highest and lowest results

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R03-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering questions about a labelled diagram

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R04 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: discuss texts with some understanding of meaning beyond the literal level, moving towards the inferential level

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R04-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between the text and their own experience or other texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R04-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting the opinion of the writer based on the ideas in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R04-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing a simple conclusion based on an information text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R05 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify and compare a range of different text types and their organisational features

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fiction and non-fiction books, based on visual and structural elements of a text such as a title, images and headings

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the different audiences and purposes associated with text types learnt in class such as fairytale, horror story, news report and information report

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the text type and purpose of a text, based on organisational features such as a sequence of ideas, headings, illustrations and layout

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the purpose and structure of texts from different curriculum areas; for example, comparing reports from Science and History or essays from English and Art

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sorting and sequencing labels for the stages of different learnt texts such as procedures and explanations

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R05-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a table or Venn diagram to compare the features of 2 text types such as narrative and blog

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R06 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the cohesion of ideas between and within paragraphs in a range of texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R06-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating the topic sentence at the beginning of each paragraph of a text, and finding the key words to identify the main idea in each paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R06-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reordering sentences in a paragraph to follow a logical order of ideas and language

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R06-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing sentences using conjunctions of time such as ‘then’, ‘next’, ‘first’ and ‘after’ to make a cohesive paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R06-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding items referred to by pronouns, and tracing these references through a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R07 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: comprehend the meaning of complex sentence patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R07-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reordering words jumbled in a sentence so that the sentence makes sense

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R07-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the meaning of a complex sentence; for example, explaining ‘He heard the explosion that wrecked the car.’ as ‘The car exploded, and the man heard it happen.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R08 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret the meaning of written text that uses a range of tenses and negation

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R08-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the base word and understanding the effect of more complex tense and negation such as in ‘had not arrived yet’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R08-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying simple passive constructions and comparing them to active constructions; for example, comparing ‘The book was read by our class.’ and ‘We read the book.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R08-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming sentences in a text into negatives or different tenses; for example, highlighting verbs in a set of provided short texts that contain present tense and changing them to past tense such as changing ‘He is running.’ to ‘He went running.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R09 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read and understand a range of descriptive language

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R09-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding an expanding range of describers and classifiers in noun groups, for example in ‘cute small animals’ and ‘introduced wild animals’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R09-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple comparatives such as ‘smaller’ and in ‘more expensive’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R10 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use knowledge of sentence structure and content to deduce the meaning of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R10-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: predicting meaning of unfamiliar words based on knowledge of the base word, for example for ‘know’, ‘unknown’ and ‘knowledge’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R10-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning of an unfamiliar word by using known contextual information or ideas in a sentence or paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R10-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of sentence structure to deduce the part of speech or function of an unfamiliar word

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R10-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that contextual and syntactical clues can be used to determine the use of homophones, for example for ‘We grow wheat on our farm.’ and ‘The train trip will take about an hour.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R11 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences to deduce the pronunciation of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R11-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: sounding out unfamiliar words using phoneme–grapheme correspondences and individual letters

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R11-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading unfamiliar words by dividing them into syllables and phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words) to identify familiar letter patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R11-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phonemic awareness and morphological knowledge (e.g. by blending and segmenting sounds, syllables and morphemes [meaningful units within words]) to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations such as ‘straightaway’ and ‘thoughtful’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R12 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and interpret direct and indirect speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R12-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the punctuation used to indicate direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R12-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a comic strip or storyboard with speech bubbles based on a passage containing direct or indirect speech

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R13 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare different types of texts across languages and cultures

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying similarities and differences between features of texts, including texts in a home language, for example in text structure, use of evidence, levels of formality and vocabulary choices

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing texts to previous experience or learning, for example ‘It’s different to my culture.’ and ‘This is only in Australia.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a Venn diagram or table with features of an English text and a home language text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying parts of an English text and a home language text that help achieve a purpose, for example when asked ‘Which parts of each text tell you when the events happened?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing characters, stereotypes, settings or events that are well known in home language stories with unfamiliar stories written in English

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R13-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in text structures or patterns of expression in home language text types, for example for an indirect argument style

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R14 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read independently for information or recreation in or outside the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R14-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting and/or borrowing a variety of texts for extended reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R14-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions about unfamiliar words and ideas, for example ‘What’s a bunyip?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R14-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing errors in pronunciation, intonation and emphasis when reading aloud, and attempting to correct these

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R14-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking assistance or feedback from peers to confirm pronunciation

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R14-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing books or other texts in a home language for information and enjoyment

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R15 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on an extensive range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an accessible English dictionary to check the meaning of unfamiliar words and/or checking meaning in a bilingual dictionary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: crosschecking meaning in English and a home language to confirm accurate understanding of key concepts and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing vocabulary found using dictionaries to classroom vocabulary lists

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to home language or bilingual texts such as glossaries, dictionaries and online translation tools for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R15-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording words and information in a personal dictionary or notes, using a combination of English and a home language to indicate meaning, pronunciation and usage

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3R16 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to shared reading activities, including personal responses to a narrow range of imaginative texts such as poems, short stories, films and/or songs

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a variety of different genres (e.g. texts with diverse characters, settings and themes), including both familiar and unfamiliar elements

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to group discussion of a text, contributing appropriate ideas and encouraging the responses of others

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E03 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating the content and form of group responses to a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E04 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining how personal experience or previous learning helps strengthen their understanding of ideas in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E05 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing new perspectives gained from reading, for example ‘I hadn’t thought about …’ and ‘I didn’t know that …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3R16-E06 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: re-reading sections of text and rehearsing reading aloud to improve fluency and understanding

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3W01 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write a range of texts that present a point of view on topics discussed in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3W01-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a structured statement of opinion, including giving context, opinion and justification

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3W01-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing and justifying a point of view about an issue in a classroom or media text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALB3W02 - EAL Pathway B
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write a range of information texts covering topics across the curriculum, incorporating information from different sources

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3W02-E01 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a narrow range of information texts used in different curriculum areas (such as historical recounts, information reports, procedures and explanations), referring to templates and models for support

elaborations.name: VC2EALB3W02-E02 - EAL Pathway B
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating information from personal experience, classroom activities and shared texts into their own writing

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level CL curriculum supports students who are beginners in English – and who may have had minimal exposure to literacy in their home language(s), and little or no prior schooling – as they develop basic knowledge, understanding and skills in English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students build their capacity to participate in routine and familiar exchanges in English with their peers. Students learn about and practise pronunciation, stress and intonation of English, and recognise how these skills impact on their clarity of expression. Through reciprocal exchanges, they develop an early awareness of the conventions of spoken English and engage in basic, sustained verbal exchanges.

Students are introduced to the English alphabet, and begin to recognise some letters and know the sounds related to common letter combinations, supported by the study of a wide range of short, familiar print and digital texts. They develop skills to decode simple texts, such as using images to support comprehension or referring to picture dictionaries and bilingual word charts to find unfamiliar words. They read aloud and apply simple strategies, such as pointing to words, to assist with fluency.

Students create short written texts. They learn about the purposes of some common text types and practise their writing using models and examples. They learn to write short texts using conventional letter formation and basic punctuation. They also learn to use digital technologies to support or construct their writing.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level CL, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students communicate using simple spoken English in familiar, structured social and classroom contexts. They use formulaic language; short, simple and well-rehearsed grammatical features; and adaptations of their emerging English repertoire. They use stress and intonation appropriately in some familiar interactions and can imitate model texts with some accuracy. They understand common instructions and questions, and simple descriptions and explanations, when strongly supported in familiar contexts. They understand and use basic subject–verb–object grammatical patterns, common regular and irregular verbs, basic prepositions and connectives such as time and sequence markers. They ask and respond to questions in predictable contexts, express simple ideas and preferences, and provide short explanations and descriptions. They use some strategies to initiate and sustain basic conversations in English, repeating and re-pronouncing as necessary.

modes.mode_body: Students read a wide range of simple, familiar fiction, information and everyday print and digital texts in handwritten, visual, multimodal and interactive formats. They complete simple structured activities about these texts. Students read their own writing and other simple texts based on well-rehearsed spoken English. They name some letters and know the sounds related to many letters and common letter combinations. They attempt to sound out words, recognise some high-frequency words and read some unfamiliar words based on the similarity of these to known words. They demonstrate awareness of basic punctuation and use stress, intonation or pausing appropriately when reading familiar texts aloud. They use simple strategies such as pointing to words as they read, or as shared texts are read aloud in class. They understand the basic practical and cultural purposes of the texts they read.

modes.mode_body: Students write short, grammatically simple texts based on well-rehearsed spoken and well-practised written English in familiar contexts. They write for a range of basic classroom and personal purposes, such as making lists and writing simple recounts and notes, and complete activities following models and examples. They recognise that print texts in English are based on certain conventions, which change according to context and purpose. Their texts use familiar sentence patterns from well-known texts or classroom models. They begin to use conventional letter formations when writing or copying text, attending to the relative sizes and shapes of letters, their position on a line and basic punctuation. They leave appropriate spaces between words. They attempt to write some unfamiliar words using their developing knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences in English, referring to personal dictionaries, glossaries and classroom resources and asking for assistance. They copy and create texts using digital tools.

elaborations.name: VC2EALCLL10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying syllables in known spoken words; for example, clapping the rhythm of ‘Mon-day’, ‘Ja-cob’ or ‘Si-en-na’

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level C1 curriculum supports students who have had some exposure to English, and to age-equivalent schooling in their home language(s) and literacy, to develop their verbal and non-verbal communication skills. Students interact with peers through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies. They actively participate in conversations, and learn about and apply formulaic language and well-rehearsed grammatical structures to initiate and sustain verbal exchanges.

Students explore a range of short, familiar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They develop decoding and comprehension skills through reading. They use simple bilingual dictionaries to find the meaning of unfamiliar words. Students discuss texts at a literal level and begin to develop inferential understanding. Students learn to draw on their expanding knowledge of English phoneme–grapheme correspondences, spoken and sight vocabulary, conventions of print text organisation and English grammar to support their reading.

Students create short written texts made up of simple sentences. They learn to express their ideas using familiar vocabulary, and modelled structures and features of other texts. They incorporate basic conventions such as headings and paragraphs to increase the fluency of their texts. They learn how to use digital technologies to support and present their written work.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level C1, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students communicate simply but effectively in English, in social and classroom contexts across the curriculum. They negotiate meaning and interact with others using formulaic language; short, simple and well-rehearsed grammatical features; and creative adaptations of their English repertoire. They use some stress and intonation appropriately in familiar interactions. They use subject–verb–object utterances, basic prepositions and some common regular and irregular verbs. They understand and use introduced vocabulary, common basic grammatical patterns and connectives such as time and sequence markers with varying grammatical accuracy to express ideas and preferences, and to provide simple explanations and descriptions. They understand simple instructions and questions, descriptions or explanations in familiar contexts and topics related to their prior knowledge and experience. They use some basic strategies to initiate and sustain conversations, including repeating or re-pronouncing as necessary.

modes.mode_body:
Students read and comprehend a range of short, simple, familiar information or fictional texts developed by the teacher. These texts may be print or digital, including handwritten, visual, multimodal and interactive texts.

Students understand a range of basic print instructions and questions in context. They discuss texts at a literal level and show some inferential understanding. They demonstrate an understanding of basic text structure, reading for different purposes, and they use titles and chapter headings to make predictions about texts. They combine their developing knowledge of English phoneme–grapheme correspondences, their developing oral and sight vocabulary, their beginning knowledge of the conventions of print text organisation in English and their emerging knowledge of English grammar to read unfamiliar texts with support. They read some common letter combinations and make logical attempts at reading unfamiliar words. They use appropriate stress, intonation and phrasing when reading known texts aloud, showing an understanding of the function of basic punctuation.

modes.mode_body: Students write for a range of basic classroom and personal purposes, including making lists and writing simple journal entries, notes, descriptions, recounts of events and instructional texts. They write simple sentences and short texts that are based on well-practised spoken English and familiar contexts. They write with varying grammatical accuracy, expressing themselves using familiar vocabulary and modelled structures and features. They order and sequence sentences about familiar topics into simple coherent texts, incorporating basic conventions such as headings and paragraphs. They correct some grammatical errors and rework drafts in response to the teacher’s suggestions. With support, they plan their texts and provide some additional information through visual texts. They use a range of strategies for finding and spelling words, using spelling patterns and checking resources. They use digital tools to write and present their texts.
