substrand_content_descriptions.text: use different verb forms, with some consistency

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of common verb tenses for familiar verbs, including present simple tense (e.g. ‘walk’ and ‘go’) and present continuous tense (e.g. ‘is walking’ and ‘is going’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some regular and common irregular past tenses, for example ‘walked’ and ‘went’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L07-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning commands with an imperative verb (e.g. ‘Come over here, please.’ and ‘Bring that.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L07-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing positive and negative statements using subject–verb constructions, for example ‘I didn’t finish.’ and ‘The bus arrived.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a small range of common descriptive language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing simple noun groups with adjectives and simple possessive pronouns, for example ‘a yellow car’ and ‘my friend’s house’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing noun groups using describers and classifiers, for example ‘tall trees’ and ‘native trees’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L08-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions such as ‘in’, ‘on’ and ‘at’ to indicate time and place, for example in ‘on Monday’ and ‘in Melbourne’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use key vocabulary and ideas from short, familiar spoken texts, supported by context

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar and learnt vocabulary in short spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using contextual information, including illustrations, vocabulary lists and print texts, to identify key ideas and predict vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L09-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recalling and applying a range of words related to familiar topics; for example, using words related to family, school, colours, numbers, days and months

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L09-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common synonyms (such as ‘fast’ and ‘quick’) and antonyms (such as ‘fast’ and ‘slow’) to communicate a range of meanings

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L09-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting a small number of words from a lexical set, for example for ‘soccer’, ‘ball’, ‘team’ and ‘match’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and reproduce pronunciation patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing common words and learnt words used in interpersonal interactions, classroom situations and content learning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: blending and segmenting sounds in words, for example ‘b-r-o-th-er’ and ‘c-l-ou-d-y’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: deleting and substituting phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words) to form new words; for example, substituting the ‘scr’ in ‘scratch’ with new initial sounds to form words such as ‘catch’, ‘batch’ and ‘hatch’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L10-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: substituting a middle sound to form a new word; for example, changing ‘stack’ to ‘stick’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and reproduce stress and intonation patterns with greater confidence and fluency

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using word stress, rhythm and intonation in familiar interactions; for example, using rising intonation for questions and stressing key words for emphasis

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising emotions indicated by changes in intonation such as anger and humour

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L11-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using strategies to support communication and engage a listener; for example, making eye contact and using facial expressions and gestures

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L11-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to audio books while following words on the page, then reading the text aloud

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify differences between aspects of spoken English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the sounds and words of English in interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L12-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to clarify differences between English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L12-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking the teacher or peers about appropriate behaviour in certain situations, for example ‘Should I use eye contact?’ and ‘Is it okay to shake hands?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L12-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the nature of social interactions with familiar people and in known settings

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: ask for repetition or clarification to confirm understanding of spoken communication and ask for help

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a listener’s body language or asking directly whether their own speech has been understood

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to re-pronounce words using different pronunciation, stress or pace

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L13-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a narrow range of simple, formulaic expressions to ask for repetition or rephrasing, for example ‘Please repeat.’ and ‘What does it mean?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for clarification from other home language speakers

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking home language peers to explain an idea in a home language and asking for a translation into English

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L14-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating questions in English and a home language to clarify classroom instructions or new ideas and vocabulary

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1L15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: listen and speak appropriately during small-group interactions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening and identifying topics and functions of group interactions such as to discuss ideas or to allocate tasks

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing a range of collaborative functions using simple language; for example, affirming (such as ‘yes’ and ‘good’), disagreeing (such as ‘no’ and ‘no good’) and staging (such as ‘next’ and ‘okay’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1L15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a home language to help learning, for example by taking notes or writing down key vocabulary

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R01 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the main themes or ideas of familiar and unfamiliar texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a narrow range of familiar text types such as simple recount, narrative and procedure

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding classroom labels, such as those on lockers or desks, and signs around the school, such as ‘front office’ and ‘toilets’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R01-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the main ideas in a range of familiar and unfamiliar texts, for example in their own writing, peers’ writing and the teacher’s writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R01-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying subject knowledge and understanding of common or learnt vocabulary to understand the main meaning of a short text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R02 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract specific information from a range of simple texts based on predictable language structures and vocabulary, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following print instructions to conduct a simple task or experiment, for example in a science lesson on magnets

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding key words in questions or instructions, and matching these to illustrations

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding information in a digital text by following hyperlinks and headings

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: dramatising or drawing parts of a story

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple or ‘true or false’ questions or sequencing information

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R02-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising key points or representing information in a visual form

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R03 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract specific information from simple charts, tables or maps, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating city or country names on a map

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in a cell of a table by using row and column headings

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R03-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing to and reading out the names of features on a labelled diagram

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use contextual cues to work out the literal meaning of unfamiliar words in a simple text, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using information in a text, such as images or descriptions, to deduce meanings

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using background or content knowledge to deduce meanings of words or phrases

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use organisational and visual elements to suggest the content of a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: categorising texts as either fiction or non-fiction

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting the purpose and audience of a range of common news media texts such as websites, news reports, opinion columns and persuasive letters

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the function of features of an instructional text such as a title, illustrations and imperative verbs

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to visuals such as text titles, supporting pictures, graphs and charts to predict and locate content in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using organisational or visual features to preview or summarise a studied text; for example, constructing a simple dot-point list or mind map

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R05-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using organisational features such as layout, illustrations and headings to find information in texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify what is being referred to by simple cohesive devices in a simple text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding common coordinating conjunctions (such as ‘and’ and ‘but’) and subordinating conjunctions (such as ‘as’ and ‘when’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching cohesive devices (such as ‘this’, ‘that’ and ‘those’) to the items they refer to

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise basic sentence and question patterns

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: ordering words and phrases to create grammatical and logical sentences and questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing out the subject, verb and object in sentences, for example in ‘She bought some fruit.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R07-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying question stems such as ‘Who’, ‘What’ and ‘Why’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise common imperatives

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and following classroom instructions containing familiar imperatives such as ‘read’, ‘answer’, ‘find out’ and ‘complete’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following simple sets of instructions, for example when asked ‘Read page one. Answer the set question.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand simple descriptive language within sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple noun groups with adjectives (such as in ‘the small chair’) and/or simple possessive pronouns (such as in ‘my brother’s bag’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding describers and classifiers in short noun groups such as ‘small animals’ and ‘wild animals’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R09-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common prepositions indicating time and place such as ‘in’, ‘on’ and ‘at’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise words for everyday items and actions, and topic-specific vocabulary that has been taught

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising in an unfamiliar text the topic-specific vocabulary that has been taught

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying topic-specific words in environmental print examples in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising words commonly used in classroom speech when they are printed in other contexts, for example on signs, on notices and in classroom texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: pronounce a range of words comprehensibly when reading aloud, based on knowledge of vocabulary and phoneme–grapheme correspondences

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing basic vocabulary or phrases accurately and reading them fluently

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: sounding out syllables and phonemes (the smallest units of sound in words) when reading unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences and familiar letter patterns to predict pronunciation

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of less common sounds and words with similar letter patterns to alter pronunciation when reading aloud

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading words with digraphs in which one letter is not pronounced (such as in ‘knife’ and ‘thumb’) and using them in writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading words with vowel digraphs (‘ee’, ‘oo’, ‘ai’, ‘ay’ and ‘ea’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R11-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using context to read the correct word when an unfamiliar word has more than one plausible pronunciation

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand simple punctuation when reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using punctuation to identify the nature of sentences; for example, identifying statements by full stops and questions by question marks

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R12-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using punctuation to identify parts of a sentence, for example by pausing appropriately at full stops and commas

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify differences in texts in English compared to home language(s)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the purpose, structure and language of cultural texts; for example, comparing a folk story in a home language to a folk story from another culture

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the structure and conventions of texts used in the classroom to texts in other languages, for example for stories in 2 languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select suitable books to read, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: skimming part of a book before selecting, to check for familiar language and ideas, illustrations and amount of print

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing books with those previously read, to predict the suitability of topic, language, length and structure

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing notes in a home language about meaning and pronunciation when encountering unfamiliar words in texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary to find translations of unfamiliar words, and noting these in a home language and English

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting help from peers or school staff who speak the same home language to find the meanings of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R15-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording spellings, meanings and translations of unfamiliar words in a personal vocabulary list

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1R16 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in teacher-led reading activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R16-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following simple print texts that are read aloud at a moderate pace

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R16-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a personal response to a text (e.g. indicating enjoyment, satisfaction, agreement or disagreement) and giving simple reasons

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R16-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing events from a text with personal experience

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1R16-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming part of a text into an unfamiliar text type; for example, creating an illustration or poem from a story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W01 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write short, simple texts for various social purposes, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a narrow range of short texts for various social purposes related to familiar experiences; for example, composing a ‘thank you’ text message or email

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using model texts and templates to structure texts appropriately

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W01-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating some formulaic expressions copied from model texts (such as ‘Dear …’ and ‘Once upon a time’) into their own writing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W02 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write short information texts on familiar content, consisting of simple sentences or statements approximating sentences

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a narrow range of short school-based text types such as descriptive, instructional and procedural texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following an appropriate structure for a text, using model texts or templates for support

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W03 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write to communicate personal ideas, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a narrow range of texts to communicate personal experiences and ideas, such as personal recounts and stories

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following the structure of model texts such as a greeting or sequence of events

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: label images using vocabulary learnt or practised in class

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling parts of a familiar diagram

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching vocabulary from a list to items in an image or features on a map

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: organise subject matter and attempt to use the structure of a specified text type

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: structuring simple stories; for example, including a beginning, a middle and an end

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing information under headings or in a template to follow a basic text structure

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: sorting jumbled sentences into groups or short paragraphs based on related topics

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W05-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping related information and sentences to create a basic paragraph, although ideas may not be sequenced clearly within the paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W05-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a topic sentence making a statement about a key idea, for example ‘Cars are bad for the environment.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use simple cohesive devices to structure writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common time and sequence markers to link and sequence ideas such as ‘Yesterday we …’ and ‘First we … Then … And then …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: including a narrow range of coordinating conjunctions such as ‘and’ and ‘but’, for example in ‘I caught a bus and then I walked.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W06-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with some common subordinating conjunctions such as ‘as’, ‘when’ and ‘until’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W06-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: employing pronouns to maintain cohesion and avoid repetition, for example in ‘Mary came to school early. She felt very tired.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use single clauses, or use simple coordinating and subordinating conjunctions to combine clauses

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing basic sentences using single words for subjects, verbs and objects in the correct order, for example ‘I learn English.’ and ‘Yesterday, we watched movies.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using noun–pronoun agreement, for example in ‘I like apples.’, with varying accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W07-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing compound sentences with a range of coordinating conjunctions such as ‘and’ and ‘but’, for example ‘They knocked on door but nobody answered.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W07-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing complex sentences using some common subordinating conjunctions such as ‘as’, ‘when’ and ‘until’, for example ‘When they arrived, they knocked on door.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC1W08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: experiment with different tenses and use some common irregular past tense verbs correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a small number of common irregular past tense verbs accurately such as ‘went’, ‘bought’ and ‘woke’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC1W08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching simple present and past tense verbs to time words, for example in ‘Today I have …’, ‘Last week we went …’ and ‘They always sit …’

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level C2 curriculum supports students who have already had 1 to 2 years of age-appropriate formal instruction in the basics of English language and literacy, and some exposure to home language literacy, to enhance their knowledge, understanding and skills in English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to initiate and negotiate topics when speaking in English, in a range of contexts. A focus on pronunciation, stress and intonation extends students’ spoken skills. In addition, they learn about ways to use paralinguistic (non-verbal) cues to support meaning.

Students explore a wide range of familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They learn to identify the main ideas in texts, and can paraphrase their understanding in spoken English. They learn strategies that help them to read unfamiliar texts and deduce the meanings of unfamiliar words, including using bilingual dictionaries to check or confirm meanings. They begin to explore basic texts and identify different reading purposes.

Students write for a range of purposes on different topics. They learn to organise their ideas and use simple sentence structures. They incorporate basic punctuation into their writing to increase the fluency of their texts. They use digital technologies to support, edit and present their written work.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level C2, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students use simple strategies for initiating communication and negotiating meaning. They communicate effectively in a range of familiar social and some basic academic contexts, experimenting with and adapting their developing English and cultural understanding. With support in academic contexts, they extract some specific information from texts and understand teacher explanations involving familiar, specific curriculum area vocabulary. With support, they use some increasingly complex grammatical features, and a basic range of connectives such as time and sequence markers, to show relationships between ideas. They use some conventional expressions to express views and attitudes. They demonstrate some understanding of the structures and features of extended texts by using appropriate stress, intonation, pauses and eye contact, and modelled introductory and concluding sentences.

modes.mode_body:
Students read and comprehend a range of short, familiar fictional and information print and digital texts and, when well supported, some unfamiliar texts. These texts include handwritten, visual, multimodal and interactive texts.

Students demonstrate comprehension beyond the literal level, by suggesting appropriate interpretations and identifying basic cultural variables where evident. They use headings and diagrams to assist in reading texts from all the curriculum areas and for a range of purposes. They extract the main ideas from information texts. They show awareness of how some connectives link and sequence ideas within a text. They read and consider the context when deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words. They read aloud with a degree of fluency, and draw on their understanding of the text to use stress and intonation with increasing accuracy. They use their developing knowledge of sentence structure and phoneme–grapheme correspondences to read unfamiliar words and self-correct. They select basic texts appropriate for specific reading purposes.

modes.mode_body: Students write for a range of everyday classroom and personal purposes, such as describing, explaining and recounting. They independently write some basic texts and experiment with presenting their own ideas. Their texts show varying spelling and grammatical accuracy. They incorporate emerging vocabulary, punctuation and grammatical features to achieve desired effects. They use an increasing range of simple connectives to indicate basic relationships within and between sentences and paragraphs. They choose appropriate text structures and use headings, tables and images. They use simple model texts as a basis for their own texts. They use strategies to organise information in supported research tasks. With teacher support and feedback, they review, redraft and improve their writing by discussing alternative ways of arranging and expressing ideas. They use a range of digital resources to write, edit and publish their texts.

elaborations.elaboration_text: using some common subordinating conjunctions such as ‘after’, ‘because’, ‘before’, ‘if’ and ‘while’ to connect clauses, for example in ‘Before you open the door, check you have your key.’ and ‘If it’s raining, I will still come.’

substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate specific information from subject-based diagrams, graphs and charts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a sentence that describes a graph or image, for example ‘More than half of the class walks to school.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading icons, menus or hyperlinks to navigate a website

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R03-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using labels or captions to identify specific features on a diagram, illustration or map

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R03-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving within or between webpages using tabs, navigation menus and hyperlinks

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R03-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using titles, headings and images to locate relevant information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use contextual cues to predict meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on contextual cues such as personal experience and knowledge of other texts to deduce meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using syntactic, logical and cultural cues to work out the meaning of unfamiliar words in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R04-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between ideas stated directly and close together; for example, linking simple cause and effect to predict a story ending

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify different text types

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the basic structure of a range of text types used at school such as narrative, informative and persuasive texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling features of layout and content organisation in a text, such as titles and chapter headings, or sequencing parts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: suggesting reasons why different audiences might read or view a text, for example ‘Teenagers might read this to study for a driving test.’ and ‘Adults might read this for safety information.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R05-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a narrow range of modelled metalanguage to name and describe features of texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand how cohesive devices organise ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating in a text a narrow range of connectives (such as ‘then’ and ‘so’), pronouns (such as ‘this’ and ‘that’) and articles (such as ‘a’ and ‘the’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying how the use of related vocabulary (synonyms, antonyms or words related to a particular topic) can make connections between parts of a text

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read texts that contain compound and complex sentences of 2 or 3 clauses

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding compound sentences that contain common coordinating conjunctions (such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’) and complex sentences that contain subordinating conjunctions (such as ‘because’, ‘if’ and ‘before’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: distinguish between verb tenses

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between verb tenses used in different text types; for example, identifying imperatives in a short recipe for making chocolate chip cookies and using past tense in a recount of a holiday

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read and understand a range of descriptive language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding an expanding range of describers and classifiers in noun groups such as in ‘cute small animals’ and ‘introduced wild animals’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding simple comparatives such as ‘smaller’ and ‘more expensive’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise common vocabulary and learnt topic-specific vocabulary from different curriculum areas

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding words learnt from classroom interactions and texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising in an unfamiliar text topic-specific vocabulary that has been learnt in other curriculum areas, for example ‘angle’, ‘primary’ or ‘foul’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: predicting the meaning of new words based on knowledge of the base word such as predicting the meaning of ‘unknown’ and ‘knowledge’ from the word ‘know’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning of an unfamiliar word by using known contextual information or ideas in the sentence or paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of sentence structure to deduce the part of speech or function of an unfamiliar word

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words based on known ideas in the sentence or paragraph

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R10-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that contextual and syntactical clues can be used to determine the use of homophones, for example ‘We grow wheat on our farm.’ and ‘The train trip will take about an hour.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences to deduce the pronunciation of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: sounding out unfamiliar words using phoneme–grapheme correspondences and individual letters

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading unfamiliar words by breaking them into syllables and phonemes to identify familiar letter patterns, including blending and segmenting sounds, syllables and morphemes to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations (such as in ‘straightaway’ and ‘thoughtful’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: understand the function of punctuation marks

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a range of punctuation marks in text such as full stops, commas, question marks, quotation marks and semicolons

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R12-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to punctuation marks when reading aloud; for example, pausing at appropriate points in the text and adjusting speech to reflect dialogue

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R12-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the punctuation used to indicate direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R12-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a comic strip or storyboard with speech bubbles, based on a passage containing direct or indirect speech

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare and contrast texts in English and home language(s)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with texts from different contexts and cultures, including school, the media, workplaces and the community

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the purpose, structure and language used in related texts in English and a home language; for example, comparing 2 news reports about the same event

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R13-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the ways in which different cultures express meaning through text, for example in ways of structuring arguments and presenting evidence

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select and read accessible yet challenging texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring an unfamiliar text by looking at content, organisational features and illustrations, and skimming a section to assess suitability

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on a home language and contextual clues to deduce meanings of unfamiliar words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a new story, with occasional prompts and corrections from the teacher

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking assistance with pronunciation from the teacher or peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing texts in a home language on classroom topics or topics of personal interest

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary or a translation app to find an English equivalent for a word known in a home language, or vice versa

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R14-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording spelling, meaning and translations of unfamiliar words in a personal vocabulary list

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words, based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an accessible English dictionary or bilingual dictionary to check the meanings of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: crosschecking meaning in English and a home language to confirm accurate understanding of key concepts and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing vocabulary found using dictionaries to classroom vocabulary lists

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R15-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to home language or bilingual texts such as glossaries, bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2R16 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in shared reading activities, expressing personal views

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R16-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a narrow range of imaginative shared texts such as poems, plays, short stories, films and songs, showing a developing understanding of key events, characters and issues

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R16-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the feelings of a character to peers through writing, illustration or role-play

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2R16-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a personal response; for example, expressing a point of view in a book club activity

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W01 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write texts for a narrow range of social purposes, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a range of texts for social purposes related to familiar and imagined experiences; for example, writing an invitation or online chat message

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple texts related to personal experiences or shared classroom activities, following structure and language in model texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W02 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write information texts for general school use, based on modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple information texts (such as reports, essays and explanations) based on model texts; for example, writing a short explanation of the water cycle

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising information into simple, logically ordered paragraphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W02-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating a narrow range of language features, including formulaic expressions and learnt words and phrases, into texts for different curriculum areas

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W03 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write some imaginative or personal texts, with support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing imaginative texts adapted from or in response to classroom texts; for example, creating a story with an alternative setting or ending

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write texts with a variety of visual forms

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in a range of visual forms such as tables, charts and graphs

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating a narrative to reflect descriptions given in the original text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W04-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions in a computer app to create tables, graphs or images

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W04-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling diagrams or filling in tables using subject-specific vocabulary

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: organise information and write according to the structure of a specified text to reflect given or new information

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: structuring simple texts in a logical form, with some independence; for example, writing a personal text with a beginning, middle and end

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: structuring more complex texts appropriately by working from a model or template

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple paragraphs and topic sentences to organise ideas in writing; for example, starting a new paragraph for a change of topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W05-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: following a model text or scaffold for paragraph structure; for example, including a topic sentence, main idea, elaboration and summary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W05-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a simple topic sentence introducing and sequencing the key ideas of a paragraph, for example ‘Another reason to ban cars is …’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: link ideas using a range of basic cohesive devices

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an expanding range of coordinating conjunctions (such as ‘and’, ‘but’ and ‘so’), for example in ‘I caught the bus and then walked to the pool so I could go swimming.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of common subordinating conjunctions (such as ‘since’, ‘because’ and ‘before’), for example in ‘Because it was getting dark, we left before the show finished.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W06-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating short chains of reference using pronouns, for example ‘The doctor … she … her patients …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W06-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns in more complex sentences, although sometimes creating ambiguity (e.g. in ‘Dad found my dog and he was so happy.’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use compound and complex sentences in developing writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing sentences with conventional word order

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing different sentence types in appropriate contexts; for example, using statements to answer questions and using commands in instructional texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W07-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing compound sentences using a range of coordinating conjunctions, for example ‘They reduce training so they can rest their muscles.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W07-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions, for example ‘Because of the flood, their homes were destroyed.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: write using a range of tenses, including simple and continuous present and past tense, with varying accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling simple and continuous present and past tenses, for example ‘They are waiting.’ and ‘I was walking.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting more complex tenses, with varying accuracy; for example, using multi-word verb groups (such as ‘was not going to say’) and elaborated tenses (such as ‘He had not been told yet.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W08-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling agreement with common subjects and simple verbs, for example ‘I go’, ‘she goes’, ‘it is’ and ‘they are’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use adverbials and prepositions to provide simple detail

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some adverbials to give simple detail about place (e.g. ‘at the station’), time (e.g. ‘last week’), accompaniment (e.g. ‘alone’), manner (e.g. ‘very quickly’) and cause (e.g. ‘because of the rain’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions with varying accuracy, for example in ‘with her parents’ and ‘in the bus’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a varied and appropriate vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from a growing range of common topic vocabulary and familiar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using subject-specific vocabulary accurately in sentences or short modelled texts such as explanations, reports and descriptions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use a narrow range of synonyms to avoid repetition and choosing vocabulary to express shades of meaning, for example ‘cloudy’, ‘gloomy’ and ‘bleak’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to use knowledge of prefixes to change the meaning of a base word such as for ‘undone’, ‘remove’ and ‘misunderstand’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying generalisations for adding affixes; for example, changing ‘hope’ to ‘hoping’, ‘begin’ to ‘beginning’ and ‘country’ to ‘countries’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W10-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some idioms learnt from reading and viewing, in creative or personal writing

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: spell most encountered words correctly, drawing on a range of strategies including graphophonic and morphemic knowledge, context clues and/or home language strategies

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning high-frequency sight words from shared texts and classroom activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common letter patterns in familiar and unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phonic knowledge and knowledge of letter patterns to spell words with 3-letter blends such as ‘str-ip’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing unfamiliar words that share common letter patterns but have different pronunciations such as ‘journey’, ‘your’, ‘tour’ and ‘sour’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of known words and base words to spell unfamiliar words; for example, knowing the spelling and meaning connections between ‘vision’, ‘television’ and ‘revision’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W11-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of spelling generalisations to spell unfamiliar words such as ‘suitable’, ‘likeable’ and ‘collapsible’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of punctuation marks consistently and correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of punctuation, such as full stops, question marks, commas and apostrophes, consistently and correctly

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W12-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using commas consistently in lists to separate clauses or indicate pauses, for example between ingredients in a recipe

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W12-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using correct punctuation in direct speech; for example, adding quotation marks to a short piece of dialogue

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: choose different forms of text and discuss their appropriateness for purpose and audience, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from a range of print and digital text types such as report, recount, description, narrative and argument

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming texts into new formats using a model text; for example, rewriting a debate as a discussion essay

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: revise and edit texts at the word, sentence and whole-text level, based on teacher or peer feedback

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to feedback at each stage of planning, drafting and editing to make improvements to text structure and language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: employing a range of strategies to check and correct spelling; for example, using dictionaries, vocabulary lists and the spellcheck function in a computer app

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting appropriate vocabulary from classroom charts, a personal dictionary and texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording subject-specific vocabulary in an organised way; for example, using a word cline, word map or labelled diagram

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: consulting resources such as bilingual dictionaries, charts, vocabulary lists, online tools, peers and the teacher to find unfamiliar words or to check spelling and meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W14-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording unfamiliar words from texts or interactions in a personal vocabulary list that includes English, a home language and other details such as meaning and phonetic pronunciation

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on a wide range of home language resources when writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words, based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an accessible English or bilingual dictionary to check the meanings of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: crosschecking meaning in English and a home language to confirm accurate understanding of key concepts and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing vocabulary found using dictionaries to classroom vocabulary lists

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W15-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to home language or bilingual texts such as glossaries, dictionaries and translation apps for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC2W16 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in shared writing activities with peers

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W16-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on their own writing through class discussion, identifying strengths and limitations of their own texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W16-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with peers in structured writing activities; for example, assessing a text against a checklist, or comparing paragraphs written by different authors

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W16-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and responding to feedback from the teacher and peers about text structure, sequencing of ideas, expression and vocabulary choices in their own writing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC2W16-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing for a writing conference with the teacher

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level C3 curriculum supports students with 2 to 3 years of age-appropriate formal instruction in English language and literacy, and some exposure to home language(s) literacy, to expand their knowledge, understanding and skills in English. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to listen, question and respond in English in a wide range of contexts. They participate in a variety of listening and speaking opportunities and develop their control of stress, rhythm and intonation during one-on-one conversations. They move beyond the literal understanding of language and start to comprehend how some abstract information is articulated in English.

Students explore a wide range of familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They learn to identify the main ideas in texts and can paraphrase their understanding in spoken English. They develop strategies that help them to read unfamiliar texts and deduce the meanings of unfamiliar words, including using bilingual dictionaries to confirm meanings and to check and extend their vocabulary. Students explore basic texts and identify different reading purposes and ways in which the structures and features of texts contribute to meaning.

Students write with a degree of autonomy for a wide range of purposes and contexts. They write independently about personal experiences and experiment with the presentation of their ideas. They learn to plan, draft, revise and edit their writing independently, as well as use increasingly advanced digital resources to create texts that are more detailed, cohesive and sequential.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level C3, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students listen, question and respond successfully in a wide range of social and academic contexts. They demonstrate sufficient control of stress, rhythm and intonation to be understood in most contexts. They use appropriate non-verbal language, take account of purpose and audience, and structure extended texts appropriately when participating in group debates and discussions. They discuss texts from across the curriculum using modelled examples in supportive classroom situations and structured group work. With varying accuracy, they use a range of question types, time signals, conjunctions and modal verbs to express points of view and to give and justify opinions. They interpret spoken and print texts and, with support, understand the full text. They listen for specific information when questions are given beforehand. They understand small amounts of abstract and generalised information when appropriate background is provided.

modes.mode_body: Students demonstrate a basic understanding of the main ideas, issues or plot developments in a range of print and digital texts across all curriculum areas. These texts include handwritten, visual, multimodal and interactive texts. Students demonstrate a basic understanding of the different purposes and structures of a range of text types and can make predictions about the likely content of texts. They identify the structure of imaginative texts they read, and the role of headings, diagrams and captions in information texts. They follow meaning across sentences and paragraphs by tracking basic cohesive and reference items, and clearly expressed cues in sentence structure and vocabulary. They use appropriate metalanguage to talk about the structure and features of a text. They adjust their rate of reading to a task, reading closely for analysis, scanning for specific information and skimming for the main idea. They use their knowledge of phoneme–grapheme correspondences and cues from surrounding text to assist in reading unfamiliar words.

modes.mode_body: Through guided activities, students write texts based on an extensive range of fictional and information text types across all curriculum areas, showing an awareness of purpose and audience. They consistently use the basic structures of these text types, and demonstrate consistent but not complete control of the English grammar appropriate to these. They demonstrate some control of passive voice, a range of tenses and direct speech. They produce paragraphs with topic sentences and incorporate some cohesive devices to make links and contrasts between and within paragraphs through a range of conjunctions, connectives and pronoun references. When planning, writing, reviewing and redrafting, they pay some attention to whole-text, sentence and word-level issues, including punctuation. They use a range of strategies when spelling unfamiliar words. They present their writing appropriately, in print and digital forms.

elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to model texts or templates to structure texts logically and construct a cohesive argument; for example, using links between ideas and providing supporting arguments

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W01-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a point of view using subjective language (such as ‘I think …’) and some objective language (such as ‘Studies have shown …’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W02-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating information from personal experience, classroom activities and shared texts into their own writing

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3W08 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: use verb forms appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate verb forms for the purpose and text type; for example, using past tense for a reflective response and passive voice in a procedural recount

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling a range of more complex verb tenses such as elaborated tenses (e.g. in ‘They had been waiting.’) and multi-word verb groups (e.g. in ‘I was not supposed to know.’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W08-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling agreement for singular and plural nouns (e.g. in ‘My brothers go to high school and my sister goes to university.’) and countable and non-countable nouns (e.g. in ‘There were clouds but there was no rain.’)

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3W09 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: use a range of expressions to qualify opinions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modalities such as ‘may’ and ‘might’ to signify opinions, for example ‘The forest may be changed by this protest action.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing formulaic expressions to introduce personal opinions, for example ‘In my view …’ and ‘I believe …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W09-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use subjective expressions to support their own opinions indirectly, for example ‘According to research …’ and ‘Many consumers think …’

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3W10 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: use a range of vocabulary to create nuance, mood and feeling

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing vocabulary purposefully for a particular effect; for example, using some learnt colloquial or idiomatic phrases and humour appropriately

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of synonyms to avoid repetition

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding differences between specialised and colloquial language, for example between ‘feline’, ‘cat’ and ‘pussycat’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: building morphemic word families and exploring word origins, for example for ‘tricycle’, ‘tripod’ and ‘triangle’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of word origins and roots, and related words, to interpret and spell unfamiliar words, and learning about how these roots affect plurals (e.g. for ‘cactus’ and ‘cacti’, ‘louse’ and ‘lice’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how some suffixes change the grammatical form of words, for example that ‘-tion’ and ‘-ment’ can change verbs into nouns, such as ‘protect’ to ‘protection’ and ‘develop’ to ‘development’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W10-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing resources to expand vocabulary; for example, using classroom texts, vocabulary lists and a print or online thesaurus

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3W13 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: understand how the purpose and audience of a text can influence content and form

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on knowledge of text types, including home language texts, to identify an appropriate text type to use; for example, writing a report to communicate information or an expositional essay to argue a point

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on previous learning, notes and templates to plan the structure of a text, showing text organisation and sequence of ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing layout and visual features to suit purpose and audience; for example, using bright colours in an illustrated story for children

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: formatting texts appropriately for purpose and audience; for example, choosing font styles, text alignment and dot points

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming texts to suit a different purpose or audience; for example, converting information on a road safety website for learner drivers to a pamphlet for older drivers

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W13-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of metalanguage related to text and language such as ‘topic sentence’, ‘verb’ and ‘pronoun’
