elaborations.elaboration_text: using a home language and English dictionary to record spelling, meaning, translation and usage in a personal vocabulary list

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words, based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W15-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording unfamiliar words in personal notes or vocabulary lists, with translations in a home language or examples from texts

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3W16 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: contribute to shared writing events

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W16-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating their own and peers’ writing with reference to model texts and editing checklists

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W16-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing language choices about purpose and audience; for example, reflecting on word choices in a persuasive text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3W16-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing for a student-led parent conference

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L01 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify the main idea in spoken texts, with some contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening actively to identify the main idea in a spoken text, based on its organisational features and/or key vocabulary, using support such as prepared questions or background information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L02 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify specific information, using question, preview and prediction strategies, with some contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key words, based on learnt vocabulary and words used in questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using support materials such as questions and print text excerpts to identify key words and sequence of information in a spoken sequence of instructions, or a verbal description or explanation relating to a topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L02-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching key information in spoken texts to print information such as transcripts and vocabulary lists

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L03 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in informal and formal spoken interactions and routines in familiar classroom situations with a narrow range of speakers, across the curriculum

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a sequence of instructions, or a simple description or explanation

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving suggestions and opinions, and asking for clarification

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L03-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating with peers or the teacher in a variety of situations, for example when planning a project or exchanging information

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L03-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in simple social conversations with peers or the teacher

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: prepare and present a formal talk with some contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using specified criteria to plan, revise, rehearse and deliver a presentation

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to various features of speech, including pronunciation, volume, pace and intonation

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L04-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to paralinguistic (non-verbal) aspects of presentation, for example by maintaining eye contact with the audience and using body language for emphasis

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L04-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and using memory aids such as palm cards and slides

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: produce a range of coherent spoken texts appropriate for audience and purpose

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing statements, questions and commands with consistent accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and producing spoken text types such as reports, arguments and formal speeches, according to conventions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating appropriate organisational features for a text type; for example, including an introduction, arguments for and against and a conclusion in a discussion

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use a range of cohesive devices to link extended speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating the relationship between events by using time signals such as ‘First …’ and ‘Later …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using extended phrases to indicate time, for example ‘Before we started the experiment, we …’ and ‘At the end of this talk, I’ll …’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L06-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending speech by constructing compound sentences using a range of coordinating conjunctions, for example ‘I went to the shops but I didn’t buy anything.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L06-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending speech by constructing complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions, for example ‘She doesn’t like fish because of the smell.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L06-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending speech by adding prepositional phrases to give additional detail, for example in ‘Without realising it was raining, he walked out the door.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use more complex verb forms accurately

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple past and present tense verbs accurately, including common irregular verbs such as in ‘I swam in the pool.’ and ‘I saw a movie on the weekend.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use a range of more complex verb forms accurately, including auxiliary verbs and negatives, for example in ‘We are going on an excursion.’ and ‘She does not want to miss out.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L07-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using passive voice based on model texts such as procedural recounts, for example ‘The equipment was collected.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L07-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with tag endings on questions, for example in ‘You didn’t tell him, did you?’ and ‘It goes back here, doesn’t it?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use longer descriptive phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of learnt subject-specific vocabulary when giving detail about a topic, using possessive pronouns, for example ‘their habitats’ and ‘its colours’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: including some simple quantifiers such as ‘some’, ‘a few’, ‘many’ and ‘any’, for example in ‘their few small habitats’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L08-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an expanding range of adjectives as describers and qualifiers, for example in ‘the bird’s unusual colours’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L08-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs and levels of possibility as modifiers to add detail to verbs, for example in ‘He trains diligently.’ and ‘She will definitely succeed.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use familiar and specific curriculum area vocabulary in spoken and/or multimodal texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating learnt vocabulary and specific curriculum area vocabulary into discussions or presentations

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using technical terms (such as ‘photosynthesis’ and ‘expiration’) and sub-technical terms (such as ‘process’ and ‘analysis’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L09-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of learnt expressions to structure a point of view, including subjective language (such as ‘I think’) and some objective language (such as ‘It is clear that …’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L09-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a narrow range of colloquial idioms learnt from interactions or texts, for example in ‘What are you doing this arvo?’ and ‘I have heaps of homework.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use pronunciation to enhance communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to accurate pronunciation when speaking in classroom situations

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising unstressed vowels in multisyllabic words such as ‘builder’ and ‘animal’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: employ a greater range of sentence stress, intonation and paralinguistic (non-verbal) skills

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating sufficient control of stress, rhythm and intonation to be understood in most situations

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting features of speech to support and convey meaning; for example, emphasising an emotion or opinion

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L11-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating as an active listener in group discussions; for example, using eye contact, facial expressions, gestures and posture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: talk about cultural differences related to spoken communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining differences between a home language and English at text, sentence and word levels

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L12-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing cultural differences in non-verbal aspects of communication such as stance, proximity, gestures and eye contact

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L12-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying cultural differences in classroom routines, including listening to others before speaking, turn-taking and putting their hand up

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L12-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with home language peers to translate and/or explain differences in concepts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: self-assess and improve aspects of spoken English language use to enhance communication

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key words in a text that may pose pronunciation problems, based on general guidance from the teacher, for example when asked ‘Highlight all the words ending in a consonant.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying specific difficulties with pronunciation, for example ‘I can’t tell the difference between “walk” and “work”.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L13-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking clarification from home language peers about new vocabulary and concepts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L13-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and justifying a point of view on a familiar topic

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L13-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing non-verbal communication for prepared presentations, for example with a partner and seeking feedback or by videoing themselves using a digital device, to enable reflection and self-assessment

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on an extensive range of home language resources when listening and speaking

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L14-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: crosschecking meaning in English and a home language to confirm accurate understanding of key concepts and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L14-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing vocabulary found using dictionaries to classroom vocabulary lists

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L14-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to home language or bilingual texts, such as glossaries, bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools, for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3L15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to collaborative group work

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a group by clarifying task goals, negotiating roles, requesting and responding to opinions, and suggesting action

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking clarifying questions in a variety of forms, for example ‘Do you mean that …?’ and ‘Could you please explain …?’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3L15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on home language resources to aid communication; for example, accessing information and taking notes

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R01 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: skim a range of texts with some contextual support for general meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a variety of common information texts that include images or diagrams

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing multimodal texts, such as news reports, that combine audio, subtitles and video

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R01-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading menus or hyperlinks to navigate a website

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R01-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing classroom texts, including a variety of information and fictional text types, in print and digital formats

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R01-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding background information associated with content and text type, including purpose and structure

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R02 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: scan a print text with some contextual support to find detailed information

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: skimming a text by identifying key words in the title, headings and topic sentences to determine the purpose and main idea of the text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: scanning a text to extract details such as names, numbers, specific words and answers to questions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R03 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: extract information from a range of visual representations, including tables, graphs and diagrams, with some teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting information in visual representations and print texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using captions, labels and topic knowledge to identify specific features on a diagram or illustration

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R03-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting bar, column and pie charts to compare different results

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R04 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use contextual cues to infer meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using existing vocabulary knowledge to predict the meaning of compound words (such as ‘daydream’) or words with familiar base words (such as ‘unbroken’)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using information in a text, such as images, headings and adjacent sentences, to deduce meaning

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R05 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare the structures of different texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: defining the functions of features in texts from different curriculum areas, such as the contents page, index, annotated diagrams and headings

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching labels to functions for different parts of a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing features of everyday or classroom texts on related topics, for example between a report and a review

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding a range of classroom text types such as practical report, review and research project

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the purpose of individual features of a text such as headings in a pamphlet or images on a website

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled metalanguage to name and describe text features

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R05-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using annotations, tables or Venn diagrams to record and communicate comparisons

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R06 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify the role of cohesive markers in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R06-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying cohesive markers in a text such as ‘also’, ‘finally’ and ‘however’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R06-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the words replaced by reference items, and tracing these reference chains through a long text such as ‘The team was reluctant to remain during the polar winter, when the sun may not be seen for over a month, as this is the most difficult time for Arctic exploration.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R07 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read texts with a range of sentence types, including complex and compound sentences with multiple clauses

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R07-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding compound and complex sentences containing multiple clauses, for example by highlighting the clauses in compound sentences such as ‘The sun was shining brightly and the birds were singing sweetly.’ and ‘I went to the shop, but I forgot my credit card.’ and in complex sentences such as ‘As the sun was setting, the children were playing in the park.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding sentences containing some sophisticated features such as noun groups and modality, for example ‘The old, broken-down car was in the street.’, ‘I can speak French.’, ‘You may leave now.’ and ‘It might rain later.’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R08 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify agent, action and consequence in sentences using passive voice

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R08-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding components of active and passive voice

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R08-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the structure of sentences in active and passive voice; for example, comparing ‘We completed the experiment.’ with ‘The experiment was completed by our group.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R08-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: converting basic active sentences into passive voice and identifying the subject, and the agent, action and consequence in the modified sentence

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R09 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: read and understand sentences containing a wide range of descriptive language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R09-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding complex noun groups that use a range of pointers, counters, describers, classifiers and qualifiers, and concrete and abstract head nouns

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R09-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding a range of adverbial phrases (such as ‘very tightly’) and prepositional phrases (such as ‘with a blue pen’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R10 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify thematic groupings of words in a text

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R10-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping or classifying words with the same topic, theme or function, for example for ‘gravity’, ‘pull’ and ‘force’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R10-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: tracing word chains that refer to a particular idea in a text, for example for ‘Junk food contains harmful additives. Salt can cause heart problems, while sugar is linked to diabetes.’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R10-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising related words to show their relationships, for example in a word cline or on a word map

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R11 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: employ a range of strategies to decode words and phrases with increasing accuracy

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R11-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of spelling conventions and phonic knowledge to unfamiliar words, for example to distinguish between ‘mat’ and ‘mate’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R11-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning an expanding repertoire of sight words from shared texts and classroom activities

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R11-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising less familiar words that share common letter patterns but have different pronunciations, for example for ‘journey’, ‘your’, ‘tour’ and ‘sour’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R12 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret an increasing range of punctuation marks

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R12-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting punctuation marks when reading aloud; for example, pausing at appropriate points in the text, and adjusting speech to reflect dialogue

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R13 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: respond to different cultural values and attitudes that are exemplified in texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R13-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying explicit and implicit representations of culture in texts, for example for descriptions of cultural practices or moral judgements based on implied cultural values

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R13-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting their own cultural knowledge with aspects represented in texts

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R13-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining familiar cultural references to others

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R14 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: select and read long complex texts, with teacher support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R14-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing a range of texts, including fiction and non-fiction, on diverse topics and with a variety of perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R14-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying texts of interest based on comprehensible structure and language, and relevant topics

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R14-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking advice from the teacher when selecting texts to read for pleasure or a specific purpose

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R14-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words and reading on to maintain fluency, and then checking unfamiliar words in a dictionary after reading

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R14-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a bilingual dictionary or translation apps to search for new vocabulary and to crosscheck meaning in a home language and English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R15 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: draw on an extensive range of home language resources when reading and viewing

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: inferring the meaning and translation of unfamiliar words, based on context and previous learning in a home language

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: making personal translations of specific words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an accessible English or bilingual dictionary to check the meanings of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: crosschecking meaning in English and a home language to confirm accurate understanding of key concepts and vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing vocabulary found using dictionaries to classroom vocabulary lists

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E06 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to home language or bilingual texts such as glossaries, bilingual dictionaries and translation apps for explanation and clarification of new vocabulary and information

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R15-E07 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a home language and English to record spelling, meaning, translation and usage in a personal vocabulary list

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC3R16 - EAL Pathway C
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to shared reading activities, including personal responses

elaborations.name: VC2EALC3R16-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a range of texts such as poems, short stories, novels, films and songs

curriculum_level_description.body:
The Level C4 curriculum supports students who have had 3 to 4 years of age-appropriate formal instruction in English language and literacy, and extended exposure to home language literacy, to expand their knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to English to make them more autonomous users of language. Through structured immersion in English and the use of plurilingual and cultural strategies, students learn to use their expanding vocabulary and knowledge of a wide range of grammatical features to engage in increasingly complex exchanges in English. They participate in a variety of listening and speaking opportunities and develop their control of stress, rhythm and intonation during verbal interactions. They move beyond the literal understanding of language and comprehend how some abstract information is articulated in English.

Students explore a variety of familiar and unfamiliar print and digital texts, including visual, multimodal and interactive texts. They learn strategies that help them to read unfamiliar texts and to deduce meanings of unfamiliar words, including using bilingual dictionaries to crosscheck meaning in their home language(s) and English. They begin to extract information from complex texts by learning how to identify key ideas. They participate in language analysis and evaluation of increasingly complex texts.

Students write with autonomy for a range of purposes. They are encouraged to develop their capacity to extend and connect their ideas and write sustained information and fictional texts. In response to feedback and self-assessment, they learn to draft and edit their writing to enhance fluency, clarity, accuracy and appropriateness for purpose, audience and context. They learn to present their writing in a range of print and digital forms.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level C4, students demonstrate the following skills in English as an Additional Language.

modes.mode_body: Students demonstrate greater autonomy and control over their use of English, combining their expanding vocabulary with the appropriate use of a wide range of complex grammatical features including modal verbs, passive voice and tenses. They demonstrate understanding of the ways in which pauses, stress, rhythm and intonation help to clarify meaning. They speak clearly and pronounce most sounds correctly. They take part in extended discourse on factual and interpersonal topics using an appropriate modelled structure, and respond appropriately to listeners’ reactions. They deliver formal and informal presentations to an audience. They identify the intention of supportive speakers, using their knowledge of how intonation, volume, stress and lexical choices support and convey meaning and emphasise opinions and emotions. They identify examples of relatively explicit subjective language. They extract information from challenging spoken texts, using guide questions and taking notes on key ideas.

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L01 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: understand the point of view and message of an unfamiliar speaker, with minimal contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L01-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening actively to other speakers to respond to or build on their contributions in discussions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using information from contextual scaffolding (such as relevant background knowledge previously provided) to identify main topics and key words

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L01-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of text structures such as introduction and topic sentences to predict key messages and recognise repeated discourse markers

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L01-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting non-verbal and evaluative language to deduce a speaker’s mood and/or feelings about a particular topic

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L02 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: extract key information or ideas from a variety of spoken texts across the curriculum, with minimal contextual support

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L02-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing and comprehending a range of cross-curricular and multimodal texts such as a guest speaker’s talk, a short film and a podcast (with captions if needed)

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L02-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking notes from short talks and mini-lectures with reduced support; for example, using broad headings rather than topic-specific questions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L02-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: listing arguments of a speaker, identifying the tone

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L03 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: participate effectively in exchanges and conversations with fluent speakers that involve changes of topic and register in the full range of classroom situations across the curriculum

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L03-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a range of classroom exchanges, including pair and group work and class discussions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L03-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating classroom exchanges for a range of purposes; for example, making statements, giving instructions, asking questions, articulating opinions, offering a suggestion and/or justification, or engaging in analysis, evaluation and/or critique

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L03-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating with peers or teachers in a wide range of situations, for example when planning work or brainstorming ideas

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L03-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to conversations with a range of people such as peers, teachers and visitors about a variety of topics, for example in discussions about family or future career

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L03-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: shifting register; for example, changing from talking about a classroom topic to making a request

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L04 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: prepare and deliver an extended formal presentation that reflects a clear progression of ideas relevant to the audience, context and purpose

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L04-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using organisational features of texts, including multimodal texts, to structure and connect complex ideas logically; for example, using topic sentences or preview and review

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L04-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an appropriate style of speech for a purpose such as to inform, persuade or entertain

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L04-E03 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and rehearsing to enhance structure, content, language and presentation style

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L04-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a piece of text, such as a persuasive text, that flows logically and cohesively, has been researched and includes well-supported arguments using sophisticated vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L04-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: speaking confidently using oral presentation skills, for example by making eye contact and using appropriate gestures, tone, register and intonation

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L05 - EAL Pathway C
content_descriptions.text: sustain complex ideas and information in coherent spoken texts, taking account of audience, context and purpose

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L05-E01 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and applying organisational features of a range of spoken texts, from informal discussions to formal spoken and multimodal presentations; for example, using appropriate structure and well-sustained arguments supported by factual details

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L05-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting a logical sequence of information in prepared and impromptu spoken texts

content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L06 - EAL Pathway C

elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronoun references to maintain cohesion throughout an extended speech

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L06-E05 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate metalanguage, for example in displays and explanations

elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from a wide range of action, saying, sensing and relating verbs such as ‘construct’, ‘produce’, ‘appreciate’ and ‘prefer’ to express precise meaning

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L07-E02 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: using extended verb groups, for example in ‘about to start packing up’ and ‘would not want to be noticed’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L07-E03 - EAL Pathway C

elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing appropriate vocabulary to construct noun groups for imaginative or informative texts, for example ‘a flock of colourful parrots’ and ‘less than 10 per cent of native seed-eating birds’

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L09-E04 - EAL Pathway C
elaborations.elaboration_text: including idiomatic and colloquial language appropriately and spontaneously in discussions

modes.mode_body:
Students compare and make judgements about different texts (such as texts on the same topic by different authors) and read a wide range of accessible and culturally appropriate texts from across the curriculum with a high degree of independence. These texts may be print or digital, including handwritten, visual, multimodal and interactive texts.

Students take notes that identify main ideas, issues and plot developments. They identify supporting information to justify a response, including significant quotations that relate to key themes. They understand the main meaning by focusing on the first lines of key paragraphs. They adjust their reading style to a task. They locate and organise information from a range of reference sources, including the internet, and begin to synthesise and make meaning from increasingly complex texts. They identify reference items across complex sentences. They predict the way a text may be organised and its likely language features. With more difficult texts, they identify a few specific facts and the basic perspective of the writer.

modes.mode_body: Students write, with appropriate support, the full range of extended imaginative and information text types undertaken across the curriculum. With support, they vary their writing to be consistent with the text type, the context and the needs of the reader, presenting similar content in different ways. They demonstrate reasonably consistent control of a wide range of grammatical features, including spelling. They incorporate direct and indirect speech, including quotations, appropriately. They employ an extended range of appropriate cohesive devices between sentences and paragraphs, retaining clarity and fluency. They use some abstract noun groups. In response to feedback and self-assessment, they review and redraft their writing to enhance fluency, clarity, accuracy and appropriateness for purpose, audience and context. They plan, draft, edit and present their writing in a range of print and digital forms, as appropriate.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2EALC4L01 - EAL Pathway C

elaborations.elaboration_text: listening actively to other speakers to respond to or build on their contributions in discussions

elaborations.name: VC2EALC4L01-E02 - EAL Pathway C
